title.tet: Pre-istória Timór nian: husi tasi okos to'o agrikultór dahuluk sira
title.pt: Pré-história de Timor: do fundo do mar aos primeiros agricultores
title.en: The prehistory of Timor: from the sea floor to the first farmers
title.id: Prasejarah Timor: dari dasar laut hingga petani pertama

summary.tet: Timór nia istória hahú iha tasi okos: ninia fatuk sira rai fósil animál tasi nian ne'ebé tuan liu tinan tokon 200. Illa ne'e sa'e husi tasi iha tinan tokon hirak ikus ne'e, no animál sira ne'ebé lakon ona, hanesan Stegodon, uluk hela iha ne'e. Maizumenus tinan 44 000 liubá ema dahuluk to'o ho ró, no maizumenus tinan 3 500 liubá sanan-rai no to'os hahú.
summary.pt: A história de Timor começa no fundo do mar: as suas rochas guardam fósseis de animais marinhos com mais de 200 milhões de anos. A ilha saiu do mar nos últimos milhões de anos e foi casa de animais hoje extintos, como o Stegodon. Há cerca de 44 000 anos chegaram de barco as primeiras pessoas, e há uns 3500 anos começaram a cerâmica e a agricultura.
summary.en: The story of Timor begins at the bottom of the sea: its rocks hold fossils of sea animals more than 200 million years old. The island rose from the sea in the last few million years and was home to animals that are now extinct, such as Stegodon. The first people arrived by boat about 44,000 years ago, and pottery and farming began about 3,500 years ago.
summary.id: Kisah Timor dimulai di dasar laut: batuannya menyimpan fosil hewan laut yang berumur lebih dari 200 juta tahun. Pulau ini muncul dari laut dalam beberapa juta tahun terakhir dan menjadi rumah bagi hewan yang kini sudah punah, seperti Stegodon. Manusia pertama datang dengan perahu sekitar 44.000 tahun lalu, dan tembikar serta pertanian dimulai sekitar 3.500 tahun lalu.

heading.pt: Uma longa história antes da escrita

text.tet: Ita bolu pre-istória ba tempu molok iha dokumentu hakerek. Testu dahuluk sira ne'ebé ko'alia kona-ba Timór mak livru Xina husi sékulu 13, tan ne'e kuaze illa ne'e nia istória tomak mak pre-istória. Atu hatene istória ne'e, sientista sira buka sinál sira. Paleontólogu sira estuda fósil, mak buat moris nia rastu ne'ebé sai fatuk ona. Arkeólogu sira ke'e fatuk-kuak no estuda ekipamentu, ruin, kulit-tasi no ahi nia rastu ne'ebé ema husik hela. Iha tempu nia sukat rua ne'ebé la hanesan: fatuk sira-nia istória ita sura ho tinan tokon, no ema sira-nia istória iha Timór ita sura ho tinan rihun, maizumenus 44 000. Ai-knanoik no lisan timoroan nian mós rai hanoin tuan sira, ne'ebé sira konta ho dalan seluk.
text.pt: Chamamos pré-história ao tempo anterior aos documentos escritos. Os primeiros textos que falam de Timor são livros chineses do século XIII, por isso quase toda a história da ilha é pré-história. Para a conhecer, os cientistas seguem pistas. Os paleontólogos estudam fósseis, restos de seres vivos transformados em pedra. Os arqueólogos escavam grutas e estudam as ferramentas, os ossos, as conchas e as cinzas que as pessoas deixaram. Há duas escalas de tempo muito diferentes: a história das rochas conta-se em milhões de anos, e a história das pessoas em Timor conta-se em milhares de anos, cerca de 44 000. As lendas e os costumes timorenses também guardam memórias antigas, contadas de outra maneira.
text.en: Prehistory is what we call the time before written documents. The first texts that mention Timor are Chinese books from the 13th century, so almost the whole history of the island is prehistory. To learn about it, scientists follow clues. Palaeontologists study fossils, the remains of living things that have turned to stone. Archaeologists dig in caves and study the tools, bones, shells and ashes that people left behind. There are two very different time scales: the story of the rocks is counted in millions of years, while the story of people on Timor is counted in thousands of years, about 44,000. Timorese legends and customs also keep old memories, told in a different way.
text.id: Prasejarah adalah sebutan untuk masa sebelum ada dokumen tertulis. Teks pertama yang menyebut Timor adalah buku-buku Tiongkok dari abad ke-13, sehingga hampir seluruh sejarah pulau ini adalah prasejarah. Untuk mengenalnya, para ilmuwan mengikuti petunjuk. Paleontolog mempelajari fosil, yaitu sisa makhluk hidup yang telah berubah menjadi batu. Arkeolog menggali gua dan mempelajari alat, tulang, cangkang kerang, dan abu yang ditinggalkan manusia. Ada dua skala waktu yang sangat berbeda: sejarah batuan dihitung dalam jutaan tahun, sedangkan sejarah manusia di Timor dihitung dalam ribuan tahun, sekitar 44.000. Legenda dan adat Timor juga menyimpan ingatan lama yang diceritakan dengan cara lain.

text.tet: Liu tinan tokon 250 liubá, fatin ne'ebé ohin Timór iha, uluk tasi okos, iha kontinente Austrália nia ninin norte. Iha períodu Pérmiku no Triásiku, krinoide (animál tasi ne'ebé hanesan ai-funan), blastoide no amonite moris iha tasi ne'e, no sira-nia rastu halo fatuk-ahu nia kamada sira. Iha Triásiku nia tasi, réptil tasi nian ida mós nani: iktiosauru. Iha tinan 2020, Institutu Jeosiénsia Timór-Leste nian (IGTL) hetan animál sira-ne'e nia ruin iha foho Lesululi, iha Kailaku (Bobonaru), no iha tinan 2026 nia fó-sai fósil sira iha ne'ebá ne'ebé karik mai husi pterosauru, réptil ida ne'ebé semo. Tempu naruk depois, iha tinan tokon hirak ikus ne'e, plaka Austrália baku malu ho Arku Banda no dudu fatuk sira-ne'e ba leten, no illa ne'e sa'e husi tasi.
text.pt: Há mais de 250 milhões de anos, o lugar onde hoje está Timor era fundo de mar, na margem norte do continente australiano. No Pérmico e no Triásico viviam nessas águas lírios-do-mar (crinoides), blastoides e amonites, e os seus restos formaram camadas de calcário. Nos mares do Triásico nadavam também répteis marinhos, os ictiossauros. Em 2020, o Instituto de Geociências de Timor-Leste (IGTL) encontrou ossos destes animais no monte Lesululi, em Cailaco (Bobonaro), e em 2026 anunciou ali possíveis fósseis de um pterossauro, um réptil voador. Muito mais tarde, nos últimos milhões de anos, a colisão da placa australiana com o Arco de Banda empurrou estas rochas para cima, e a ilha saiu do mar.
text.en: More than 250 million years ago, the place where Timor is today was sea floor, on the northern edge of the Australian continent. In the Permian and Triassic periods, sea lilies (crinoids), blastoids and ammonites lived in these waters, and their remains formed layers of limestone. Marine reptiles called ichthyosaurs also swam in the Triassic seas. In 2020 the Timor-Leste Institute of Geosciences (Instituto de Geociências de Timor-Leste, IGTL) found bones of these animals on Mount Lesululi, in Cailaco (Bobonaro), and in 2026 it announced possible fossils of a pterosaur, a flying reptile, from the same place. Much later, in the last few million years, the collision of the Australian plate with the Banda Arc pushed these rocks up, and the island rose out of the sea.
text.id: Lebih dari 250 juta tahun lalu, tempat Timor berada sekarang adalah dasar laut di tepi utara benua Australia. Pada zaman Perm dan Trias, lili laut (krinoid), blastoid, dan amonit hidup di perairan itu, dan sisa-sisanya membentuk lapisan batu kapur. Di laut zaman Trias juga berenang reptil laut, yaitu iktiosaurus. Pada 2020, Institut Geosains Timor-Leste (Instituto de Geociências de Timor-Leste, IGTL) menemukan tulang hewan-hewan ini di Gunung Lesululi, Cailaco (Bobonaro), dan pada 2026 lembaga itu mengumumkan temuan fosil yang mungkin berasal dari pterosaurus, reptil terbang, di tempat yang sama. Jauh kemudian, dalam beberapa juta tahun terakhir, tabrakan lempeng Australia dengan Busur Banda mendorong batuan ini ke atas, dan pulau ini muncul dari laut.

heading.tet: Animál sira husi illa ida ne'ebé mesak

text.tet: Tanba tasi kle'an haleu Timór nafatin, animál sira ne'ebé bele nani, semo ka namlele de'it mak to'o illa ne'e. Iha illa sira, animál boot balu sai ki'ik no animál ki'ik balu sai boot tebes. Timór iha Stegodon timorensis, elefante nia família ki'ik ida, lenuk boot sira ne'ebé hela iha rai-maran, no laho boot sira ne'ebé bele todan maizumenus kg 5. Stegodon nia nehan-naruk ida ne'ebé sientista sira sukat ona nia idade hatudu katak animál sira-ne'e hela iha Timór tinan 130 000 liubá ka uluk liu, molok ema to'o. Maibé laho boot sira moris hamutuk ho ema durante tinan rihun barak, no lakon de'it iha tinan rihun hirak ikus ne'e, bainhira ema ko'a ai-laran barak.
text.pt: Como Timor sempre esteve rodeada de mar profundo, só chegavam à ilha animais capazes de nadar, voar ou flutuar. Nas ilhas, alguns animais grandes ficam mais pequenos e alguns pequenos ficam enormes. Timor teve o Stegodon timorensis, um pequeno parente dos elefantes, tartarugas-gigantes terrestres e ratos gigantes que podiam pesar cerca de 5 kg. Uma presa de stegodon datada mostra que estes animais viviam em Timor há 130 000 anos ou mais, muito antes das pessoas. Os ratos gigantes, pelo contrário, conviveram com as pessoas durante dezenas de milhares de anos e só desapareceram nos últimos milhares de anos, quando grande parte da floresta foi cortada.
text.en: Because Timor has always been surrounded by deep sea, only animals that could swim, fly or float reached the island. On islands, some large animals become smaller and some small animals become huge. Timor had Stegodon timorensis, a small relative of elephants, giant land tortoises, and giant rats that could weigh about 5 kg. A dated stegodon tusk shows that these animals lived on Timor 130,000 years ago or earlier, long before people. The giant rats, on the other hand, lived alongside people for tens of thousands of years and disappeared only in the last few thousand years, when much of the forest was cut down.
text.id: Karena Timor selalu dikelilingi laut dalam, hanya hewan yang mampu berenang, terbang, atau mengapung yang sampai ke pulau ini. Di pulau, sebagian hewan besar menjadi lebih kecil dan sebagian hewan kecil menjadi sangat besar. Timor pernah memiliki Stegodon timorensis, kerabat kecil gajah, kura-kura darat raksasa, dan tikus raksasa yang beratnya bisa mencapai sekitar 5 kg. Sebuah gading stegodon yang sudah ditentukan umurnya menunjukkan bahwa hewan ini hidup di Timor 130.000 tahun lalu atau lebih awal, jauh sebelum manusia datang. Sebaliknya, tikus raksasa hidup berdampingan dengan manusia selama puluhan ribu tahun dan baru punah dalam beberapa ribu tahun terakhir, ketika sebagian besar hutan ditebang.

heading.pt: As primeiras pessoas e as grutas
heading.en: The first people and the caves

text.tet: Ema dahuluk to'o Timór maizumenus tinan 44 000 liubá, tuir ke'e sira iha fatuk-kuak Laili, iha Manatutu. Sira mai liu tasi, tanba Timór nunka liga ho Ázia ka Austrália liuhusi rai-maran. Sira moris husi kaer ikan, foti kulit-tasi no kasa animál, no sira hela iha fatuk-kuak sira husi fatuk-ahu. Iha Jerimalai, besik Tutuala, iha atun nia ruin ho idade maizumenus tinan 42 000, no anzól kulit-tasi tuan tebes. Iha fatuk-kuak sira Lautein nian, hanesan Lene Hara no Ili Kére Kére, didin sira iha liman nia marka, ema nia oin ne'ebé ema ko'a iha fatuk, no pintura ró, ema no animál nian, ne'ebé ema halo durante tinan rihun barak.
text.pt: As primeiras pessoas chegaram a Timor há cerca de 44 000 anos, segundo as escavações do abrigo de Laili, em Manatuto. Vieram por mar, porque Timor nunca esteve ligada por terra à Ásia nem à Austrália. Viviam da pesca, da apanha de marisco e da caça, e abrigavam-se em grutas de calcário. Em Jerimalai, perto de Tutuala, há ossos de atum com cerca de 42 000 anos e anzóis de concha muito antigos. Nas grutas de Lautém, como Lene Hara e Ili Kére Kére, as paredes têm mãos em negativo, rostos gravados na rocha e pinturas de barcos, pessoas e animais, feitas ao longo de milhares de anos.
text.en: The first people reached Timor about 44,000 years ago, according to excavations at the Laili rock shelter in Manatuto. They came by sea, because Timor was never joined by land to Asia or Australia. They lived by fishing, gathering shellfish and hunting, and they sheltered in limestone caves. At Jerimalai, near Tutuala, there are tuna bones about 42,000 years old and very old fish hooks made of shell. In the caves of Lautém, such as Lene Hara and Ili Kére Kére, the walls have hand stencils, faces carved into the rock and paintings of boats, people and animals, made over thousands of years.
text.id: Manusia pertama tiba di Timor sekitar 44.000 tahun lalu, menurut penggalian di ceruk batu Laili, Manatuto. Mereka datang lewat laut, karena Timor tidak pernah tersambung lewat daratan dengan Asia maupun Australia. Mereka hidup dari menangkap ikan, mengumpulkan kerang, dan berburu, serta berlindung di gua-gua batu kapur. Di Jerimalai, dekat Tutuala, terdapat tulang ikan tuna berumur sekitar 42.000 tahun dan kail dari cangkang kerang yang sangat tua. Di gua-gua Lautém, seperti Lene Hara dan Ili Kére Kére, dindingnya memuat cap tangan, wajah yang dipahat di batu, serta lukisan perahu, manusia, dan hewan yang dibuat selama ribuan tahun.

heading.pt: Agricultores, metal e os primeiros escritos
heading.en: Farmers, metal and the first written records

text.tet: Maizumenus tinan 3 500 liubá, sanan-rai mosu iha fatuk-kuak sira Timór-Leste nian, no la kleur depois animál sira ne'ebé ema lori ho ró mós mosu, hanesan asu. Iha tempu ne'e, ema ne'ebé ko'alia lian Austronézia to'o, no to'os no hakiak animál namkari. Tinan 2 000 liubá ka uluk liu, sasán bronze mós to'o: iha tinan 2014, ema hetan iha Baukau tambór boot ida tipu Dong Son, ne'ebé mai husi área Vietname no Xina nia sul. Husi sékulu 13, livru Xina sira ko'alia kona-ba Timór no ninia ai-kameli, no iha tinan 1365 poema ida husi Java tau illa ne'e iha rai sira-nia lista ne'ebé liga ho Majapahit. Iha tinan 1522, Antonio Pigafetta, husi Fernão de Magalhães nia espedisaun, hakerek relatóriu dahuluk husi ema Europa ida ne'ebé to'o duni illa ne'e.
text.pt: Há cerca de 3500 anos aparece a cerâmica nas grutas de Timor-Leste e, pouco depois, animais trazidos de barco, como o cão. É a época em que chegam falantes de línguas austronésias e se espalham a agricultura e a criação de animais. Há uns 2000 anos ou mais chegam também objetos de bronze: em 2014 encontrou-se em Baucau um grande tambor do tipo Dong Son, vindo da região do atual Vietname e do sul da China. A partir do século XIII, livros chineses falam de Timor e do seu sândalo, e em 1365 um poema de Java inclui a ilha entre as terras ligadas a Majapahit. Em 1522, Antonio Pigafetta, da expedição de Fernão de Magalhães, deixou o primeiro relato de um europeu que esteve na ilha.
text.en: About 3,500 years ago pottery appears in the caves of Timor-Leste and, soon after, animals brought by boat, such as the dog. This is the time when speakers of Austronesian languages arrive and farming and animal keeping spread. Some 2,000 years ago or earlier, bronze objects also arrive: in 2014 a large Dong Son-type drum, which came from the region of present-day Vietnam and southern China, was found in Baucau. From the 13th century, Chinese books mention Timor and its sandalwood, and in 1365 a poem from Java lists the island among the lands linked to Majapahit. In 1522 Antonio Pigafetta, of Ferdinand Magellan's expedition, wrote the first account by a European who had been on the island.
text.id: Sekitar 3.500 tahun lalu, tembikar muncul di gua-gua Timor-Leste, dan tak lama kemudian muncul hewan yang dibawa dengan perahu, seperti anjing. Inilah masa ketika penutur bahasa Austronesia datang, dan pertanian serta peternakan menyebar. Sekitar 2.000 tahun lalu atau lebih awal, benda-benda perunggu juga tiba: pada 2014 sebuah nekara besar tipe Dong Son, yang berasal dari wilayah Vietnam dan Tiongkok selatan sekarang, ditemukan di Baucau. Sejak abad ke-13, buku-buku Tiongkok menyebut Timor dan cendananya, dan pada 1365 sebuah syair dari Jawa mencantumkan pulau ini di antara negeri yang terkait dengan Majapahit. Pada 1522, Antonio Pigafetta, anggota ekspedisi Ferdinand Magelhaens, menulis catatan pertama dari seorang Eropa yang pernah berada di pulau ini.

summary.tet: Uluk liu molok Timór iha, ninia fatuk sira mak rai-tahu, rai-henek no kulit-tasi iha tasi okos. Tan ne'e Timór famozu iha mundu tanba fósil tasi nian husi Pérmiku no Triásiku, hanesan krinoide, blastoide no amonite. Iha Triásiku nia tasi mós moris iktiosauru, réptil ho forma hanesan golfiñu, no ema hetan sira-nia ruin iha foho Lesululi.
summary.pt: Muito antes de Timor existir, as suas rochas eram lama, areia e conchas no fundo do mar. Por isso, Timor é famosa no mundo pelos fósseis marinhos do Pérmico e do Triásico, como lírios-do-mar, blastoides e amonites. Nos mares do Triásico viviam também ictiossauros, répteis com forma de golfinho, cujos ossos foram encontrados no monte Lesululi.
summary.en: Long before Timor existed, its rocks were mud, sand and shells on the sea floor. That is why Timor is famous around the world for marine fossils from the Permian and Triassic periods, such as sea lilies, blastoids and ammonites. Ichthyosaurs, dolphin-shaped reptiles, also lived in the Triassic seas, and their bones have been found on Mount Lesululi.
summary.id: Jauh sebelum Timor ada, batuannya adalah lumpur, pasir, dan cangkang di dasar laut. Karena itu, Timor terkenal di dunia berkat fosil laut dari zaman Perm dan Trias, seperti lili laut, blastoid, dan amonit. Di laut zaman Trias juga hidup iktiosaurus, reptil berbentuk lumba-lumba, yang tulangnya ditemukan di Gunung Lesululi.

heading.tet: Tasi tuan ida iha Austrália nia ninin
heading.pt: Um mar antigo na margem da Austrália
heading.en: An ancient sea on the edge of Australia

text.tet: Iha períodu Pérmiku, maizumenus tinan tokon 299 to'o 252 liubá, kuaze kontinente hotu hamutuk iha superkontinente ida naran Panjeia. Área ne'ebé ohin mak Timór uluk iha tasi ida ne'ebé la kle'an nia okos, besik rai ne'ebé depois sai Austrália nia ninin norte. Iha tasi ne'e, ahu-ruin, kulit-tasi no animál barak ho ruin husi fatuk-ahu moris. Bainhira sira mate, sira-nia parte toos halibur iha tasi okos, no ho tempu sai toos no sai fatuk-ahu. Iha Timór, fatuk balu kuaze hotu halo husi fósil nia pedasuk ki'ik sira. Iha Timór-Leste, fatuk-ahu husi tempu ne'e mosu, ezemplu, iha Formasaun Maubisse, kahur ho fatuk foho-ahi tuan sira.
text.pt: No período Pérmico, há cerca de 299 a 252 milhões de anos, quase todos os continentes estavam unidos num supercontinente chamado Pangeia. A região que hoje é Timor ficava debaixo de um mar pouco fundo, junto à margem norte da terra que mais tarde seria a Austrália. Nesse mar viviam corais, conchas e muitos animais com esqueleto de calcário. Quando morriam, as suas partes duras acumulavam-se no fundo e, com o tempo, endureciam e formavam calcário. Em algumas rochas de Timor quase tudo são bocadinhos de fósseis. Em Timor-Leste, calcários desta idade aparecem, por exemplo, na Formação de Maubisse, misturados com rochas vulcânicas antigas.
text.en: In the Permian period, about 299 to 252 million years ago, almost all the continents were joined in a supercontinent called Pangaea. The area that is Timor today lay under a shallow sea, close to the northern edge of the land that would later become Australia. Corals, shelled animals and many other creatures with limestone skeletons lived in this sea. When they died, their hard parts piled up on the sea floor and, over time, hardened into limestone. Some rocks on Timor are made almost entirely of tiny pieces of fossils. In Timor-Leste, limestones of this age appear, for example, in the Maubisse Formation, mixed with old volcanic rocks.
text.id: Pada zaman Perm, sekitar 299 sampai 252 juta tahun lalu, hampir semua benua menyatu dalam sebuah superbenua bernama Pangea. Wilayah yang kini menjadi Timor berada di bawah laut dangkal, dekat tepi utara daratan yang kelak menjadi Australia. Di laut itu hidup karang, hewan bercangkang, dan banyak hewan lain yang berkerangka kapur. Ketika mati, bagian tubuhnya yang keras menumpuk di dasar laut dan, seiring waktu, mengeras menjadi batu kapur. Sebagian batuan di Timor hampir seluruhnya tersusun dari kepingan kecil fosil. Di Timor-Leste, batu kapur seumur itu muncul, misalnya, di Formasi Maubisse, bercampur dengan batuan gunung api tua.

text.tet: Krinoide hanesan ai-funan, maibé sira mak animál, família ho fitun-tasi. Sira iha ain naruk ida, isin ida ho forma hanesan kopu, no liman sira ne'ebé kaer hahán iha bee laran; to'o ohin loron krinoide sei moris iha tasi. Blastoide mak sira-nia família, ho isin ki'ik ida ne'ebé hanesan ai-funan ne'ebé seidauk nakfera, no sira lakon ba nafatin iha Pérmiku nia rohan. Fatuk Pérmiku Timór nian fó fósil sira-ne'e barak tebes, husi espésie oioin, no sira iha fatuk riku liu balu iha mundu. Espedisaun Europa nian sira foti fósil barak iha sékulu 20 nia hahú, no ohin loron sira iha muzeu sira. Fatin klásiku famozu liu sira iha Timór loro-monu, iha Indonézia, maibé fatuk ho idade hanesan kontinua iha Timór-Leste.
text.pt: Os crinoides, ou lírios-do-mar, parecem flores, mas são animais, parentes das estrelas-do-mar. Têm um pé comprido, um corpo em forma de taça e braços que apanham comida na água; ainda hoje há crinoides nos oceanos. Os blastoides eram seus parentes, com um corpo pequeno em forma de botão de flor, e desapareceram para sempre no fim do Pérmico. As rochas pérmicas de Timor deram enormes quantidades destes fósseis, de muitas espécies, e estão entre as mais ricas do mundo. Muitos foram recolhidos no início do século XX por expedições europeias e estão hoje em museus. Os sítios clássicos mais famosos ficam em Timor Ocidental, na Indonésia, mas rochas da mesma idade continuam em Timor-Leste.
text.en: Crinoids, or sea lilies, look like flowers, but they are animals, relatives of starfish. They have a long stalk, a cup-shaped body and arms that catch food from the water; crinoids still live in the oceans today. Blastoids were their relatives, with a small body shaped like a flower bud, and they died out forever at the end of the Permian. Timor's Permian rocks have yielded huge numbers of these fossils, of many species, and are among the richest in the world. Many were collected in the early 20th century by European expeditions and are now in museums. The most famous classic sites are in West Timor, in Indonesia, but rocks of the same age continue into Timor-Leste.
text.id: Krinoid, atau lili laut, tampak seperti bunga, tetapi sebenarnya hewan, kerabat bintang laut. Krinoid memiliki tangkai panjang, tubuh berbentuk cawan, dan lengan yang menangkap makanan dari air; sampai sekarang krinoid masih hidup di samudra. Blastoid adalah kerabatnya, dengan tubuh kecil berbentuk kuncup bunga, dan punah untuk selamanya pada akhir zaman Perm. Batuan Perm di Timor menghasilkan sangat banyak fosil seperti ini, dari banyak spesies, dan termasuk yang terkaya di dunia. Banyak di antaranya dikumpulkan pada awal abad ke-20 oleh ekspedisi-ekspedisi Eropa dan kini disimpan di museum. Situs-situs klasik yang paling terkenal berada di Timor Barat, Indonesia, tetapi batuan yang seumur berlanjut ke Timor-Leste.

text.tet: Amonite mak lula no polvu nia família. Sira iha kulit ida ne'ebé lolon hanesan espirál, fahe ba kuartu ki'ik sira ho gás ne'ebé ajuda sira atu namlele. Sira muda lalais tuir tempu, tan ne'e espésie ida-idak ajuda jeólogu sira atu hatene fatuk kamada ida nia idade. Timór iha amonite husi Pérmiku no Triásiku. Entre períodu rua ne'e, maizumenus tinan tokon 252 liubá, akontese lakon boot liu iha Rai nia istória: espésie tasi nian barak liu mate hotu, inklui blastoide sira. Amonite sira mós kuaze lakon hotu, maibé balu moris nafatin no namkari fali iha Triásiku nia tasi.
text.pt: As amonites eram parentes das lulas e dos polvos. Tinham uma concha enrolada em espiral, dividida em câmaras com gás que as ajudavam a flutuar. Mudavam depressa ao longo do tempo, por isso cada espécie ajuda os geólogos a saber a idade de uma camada de rocha. Timor tem amonites do Pérmico e do Triásico. Entre os dois períodos, há cerca de 252 milhões de anos, deu-se a maior extinção da história da Terra: desapareceu a maior parte das espécies do mar, incluindo os blastoides. As amonites quase desapareceram também, mas algumas sobreviveram e voltaram a espalhar-se pelos mares do Triásico.
text.en: Ammonites were relatives of squid and octopuses. They had a shell coiled in a spiral, divided into chambers filled with gas that helped them float. They changed quickly over time, so each species helps geologists to tell the age of a rock layer. Timor has ammonites from the Permian and the Triassic. Between the two periods, about 252 million years ago, came the greatest extinction in Earth's history: most species in the sea disappeared, including the blastoids. Ammonites nearly disappeared too, but some survived and spread again through the Triassic seas.
text.id: Amonit adalah kerabat cumi-cumi dan gurita. Amonit memiliki cangkang yang melingkar seperti spiral, terbagi menjadi ruang-ruang berisi gas yang membantunya mengapung. Amonit berubah dengan cepat dari waktu ke waktu, sehingga setiap spesiesnya membantu ahli geologi mengetahui umur suatu lapisan batuan. Timor memiliki amonit dari zaman Perm dan Trias. Di antara kedua zaman itu, sekitar 252 juta tahun lalu, terjadi kepunahan terbesar dalam sejarah Bumi: sebagian besar spesies laut lenyap, termasuk blastoid. Amonit juga hampir punah, tetapi sebagian bertahan dan kembali menyebar di laut zaman Trias.

text.tet: Depois lakon boot ne'e, réptil sira manán tasi. Iktiosauru iha isin hanesan golfiñu, ibun naruk no barbatana; sira dada iis ho ar no hahoris oan moris, la hatolun. Iha tinan 1935, paleontólogu E. von Huene deskreve nehan balu husi Timór hanesan mozasauru nian, réptil tasi seluk ida ne'ebé foun liu. Estudu ida depois hatudu katak nehan sira-ne'e mai husi iktiosauru ida husi Triásiku. Iha tinan 2020, ekipa ida husi Institutu Jeosiénsia Timór-Leste nian (IGTL) hetan iktiosauru nia ruin iha foho Lesululi, iha Kailaku, Bobonaru. Notísia sira dehan katak ruin sira-ne'e tuan liu tinan tokon 200. Estudu ne'e la'o nafatin hamutuk ho muzeu no universidade husi Suésia, Noruega no Austrália.
text.pt: Depois da grande extinção, os répteis conquistaram o mar. Os ictiossauros tinham corpo de golfinho, focinho comprido e barbatanas; respiravam ar e davam à luz crias vivas, sem pôr ovos. Em 1935, o paleontólogo E. von Huene descreveu dentes de Timor como sendo de um mosassauro, um réptil marinho muito mais recente. Um estudo posterior mostrou que eram de um ictiossauro do Triásico. Em 2020, uma equipa do Instituto de Geociências de Timor-Leste (IGTL) encontrou ossos de ictiossauro no monte Lesululi, em Cailaco, Bobonaro. As notícias dão-lhes mais de 200 milhões de anos. O estudo continua com museus e universidades da Suécia, da Noruega e da Austrália.
text.en: After the great extinction, reptiles conquered the sea. Ichthyosaurs had a dolphin-like body, a long snout and flippers; they breathed air and gave birth to live young instead of laying eggs. In 1935 the palaeontologist E. von Huene described teeth from Timor as belonging to a mosasaur, a much younger marine reptile. A later study showed that they came from a Triassic ichthyosaur. In 2020 a team from the Timor-Leste Institute of Geosciences (Instituto de Geociências de Timor-Leste, IGTL) found ichthyosaur bones on Mount Lesululi, in Cailaco, Bobonaro. News reports say they are more than 200 million years old. The study continues with museums and universities in Sweden, Norway and Australia.
text.id: Setelah kepunahan besar itu, reptil menguasai laut. Iktiosaurus bertubuh seperti lumba-lumba, bermoncong panjang, dan bersirip; hewan ini bernapas dengan udara dan melahirkan anak, bukan bertelur. Pada 1935, paleontolog E. von Huene menggambarkan gigi-gigi dari Timor sebagai gigi mosasaurus, reptil laut yang jauh lebih muda. Penelitian kemudian menunjukkan bahwa gigi itu berasal dari iktiosaurus zaman Trias. Pada 2020, tim dari Institut Geosains Timor-Leste (Instituto de Geociências de Timor-Leste, IGTL) menemukan tulang iktiosaurus di Gunung Lesululi, Cailaco, Bobonaro. Menurut berita, umurnya lebih dari 200 juta tahun. Penelitian ini berlanjut bersama museum dan universitas dari Swedia, Norwegia, dan Australia.

text.tet: Fósil la'ós buat furak de'it. Sira ajuda jeólogu sira atu hatene fatuk sira-nia idade no komprende oinsá Timór mosu, no informasaun ne'e mós útil atu buka bee, mina-rai no gás. Fósil mós hatudu oinsá moris muda depois krize boot sira iha Rai. Fósil mak patrimóniu: bainhira ema hakotu sira, ka fa'an sira ba rai li'ur, informasaun ne'ebé sira rai lakon. Tan ne'e, IGTL hakarak proteje fatin importante sira nu'udar patrimóniu jeolójiku, no propoin foho Lesululi ba jeoparke ida ne'ebé UNESCO rekoñese. Se ó hetan fatuk ida ho forma estranu, foti foto, hakerek fatin ne'e no fó-hatene ba profesór ka autoridade sira, la'ós hakotu fatuk ne'e.
text.pt: Os fósseis não são só curiosidades. Ajudam os geólogos a datar as rochas e a perceber como Timor se formou, uma informação útil também para procurar água, petróleo e gás. Mostram ainda como a vida mudou depois de grandes crises da Terra. Os fósseis são património: quando são partidos, ou vendidos para fora do país, perde-se a informação que guardam. Por isso, o IGTL quer proteger os locais mais importantes como património geológico e propôs o monte Lesululi para um geoparque reconhecido pela UNESCO. Se encontrar uma pedra com formas estranhas, fotografe-a, anote o lugar e avise os professores ou as autoridades, em vez de a partir.
text.en: Fossils are not just curiosities. They help geologists to date rocks and to understand how Timor was formed, information that is also useful when searching for water, oil and gas. They also show how life changed after great crises on Earth. Fossils are heritage: when they are broken, or sold abroad, the information they hold is lost. That is why the IGTL wants to protect the most important sites as geological heritage and has proposed Mount Lesululi for a UNESCO-recognised geopark. If you find a stone with strange shapes, photograph it, note the place and tell your teachers or the authorities, instead of breaking it.
text.id: Fosil bukan sekadar benda aneh. Fosil membantu ahli geologi menentukan umur batuan dan memahami bagaimana Timor terbentuk, informasi yang juga berguna untuk mencari air, minyak bumi, dan gas. Fosil juga menunjukkan bagaimana kehidupan berubah setelah krisis-krisis besar di Bumi. Fosil adalah warisan: jika dipecahkan atau dijual ke luar negeri, informasi yang disimpannya hilang. Karena itu, IGTL ingin melindungi situs-situs terpenting sebagai warisan geologi dan telah mengusulkan Gunung Lesululi menjadi geopark yang diakui UNESCO. Jika menemukan batu dengan bentuk aneh, potretlah batu itu, catat tempatnya, dan beri tahu guru atau pihak berwenang, jangan memecahkannya.

review.notes: Crinoid, blastoid and ammonite biology is general palaeontology; Timor's Permian/Triassic setting follows the ANU 'Permian of Timor' and 'Triassic of Timor' records. From general knowledge, to check: 'enormous quantities… among the richest in the world', 'collected by early-20th-century European expeditions and now in museums' (e.g. Wanner's 'Paläontologie von Timor', the Dutch Timor expeditions), 'classic sites in West Timor' (e.g. Basleo), and Permian limestones of the Maubisse Formation with old volcanic rocks (as in tl.land.geology). The text avoids calling the Permian sea 'warm' (Timor's Permian latitude is debated). 1935 teeth: from the title of the Neues Jahrbuch paper ('Globidens timorensis E. von Huene 1935 not a durophagous mosasaur but an enigmatic Triassic ichthyosaur'); von Huene's first name and the year of the reinterpretation were not checked. text.tet: Iha 11 Agostu 2026, ajénsia notísia Tatoli publika katak IGTL estuda hela fósil sira ne'ebé karik mai husi pterosauru iha foho Lesululi, iha postu administrativu Kailaku, munisípiu Bobonaru. Ekipa ne'e hetan fósil sira iha Jullu 2026, bainhira sira kontinua serbisu iha fatin ne'e kona-ba iktiosauru nia ruin. IGTL nia prezidente, Job Brites dos Santos, esplika katak identifikasaun ne'e seidauk final, no presiza análize sientífika tan atu konfirma. Sientista sira estuda hela amostra sira iha Suésia, no depois amostra sira sei fila fali mai Timór-Leste. Iha ne'ebá IGTL hakarak harii fali fósil sira no hatudu sira iha muzeu ida.
text.pt: A 11 de agosto de 2026, a agência noticiosa Tatoli publicou que o IGTL estava a estudar possíveis fósseis de pterossauro no monte Lesululi, no posto administrativo de Cailaco, município de Bobonaro. Os fósseis foram encontrados em julho de 2026, durante os trabalhos que continuavam no mesmo lugar sobre os ossos de ictiossauro. O presidente do IGTL, Job Brites dos Santos, explicou que a identificação ainda é provisória e que é preciso mais análise científica para a confirmar. As amostras estão a ser estudadas na Suécia e deverão depois voltar a Timor-Leste, onde o IGTL quer reconstruir os fósseis e mostrá-los num museu.
text.en: On 11 August 2026 the Tatoli news agency reported that the IGTL was studying possible pterosaur fossils on Mount Lesululi, in Cailaco administrative post, Bobonaro municipality. The fossils were found in July 2026, during continuing work at the same site on the ichthyosaur bones. The IGTL's president, Job Brites dos Santos, explained that the identification is still provisional and that more scientific analysis is needed to confirm it. The samples are being studied in Sweden and are then due to return to Timor-Leste, where the IGTL wants to reconstruct the fossils and display them in a museum.
text.id: Pada 11 Agustus 2026, kantor berita Tatoli memberitakan bahwa IGTL sedang meneliti fosil yang mungkin berasal dari pterosaurus di Gunung Lesululi, pos administratif Cailaco, munisipalitas Bobonaro. Fosil-fosil itu ditemukan pada Juli 2026, ketika pekerjaan di tempat yang sama mengenai tulang iktiosaurus masih berlanjut. Presiden IGTL, Job Brites dos Santos, menjelaskan bahwa identifikasi ini masih sementara dan perlu analisis ilmiah lebih lanjut untuk memastikannya. Sampel-sampelnya sedang diteliti di Swedia dan nantinya akan kembali ke Timor-Leste, tempat IGTL ingin merekonstruksi fosil itu dan memamerkannya di sebuah museum.

text.tet: Pterosauru sira mak réptil ne'ebé semo, no sira moris maizumenus tinan tokon 228 to'o 66 liubá, iha dinosauru sira-nia tempu. Sira mak animál dahuluk ho ruin-kotuk ne'ebé semo ho liras ne'ebé sira book, uluk liu manu no niki sira. Sira-nia liras mak kulit mihis ida ne'ebé kesi ba liman-fuan dahaat ne'ebé naruk tebes. Sira-nia ruin mamuk no kmaan. Balu ki'ik hanesan manu ki'ik ida; seluk iha liras ho naruk maizumenus metru 10 husi rohan ida ba rohan seluk. Hanoin didi'ak: pterosauru la'ós dinosauru no la'ós manu, maibé sira mak dinosauru sira-nia família besik. Tan ne'e, maski sientista sira konfirma identifikasaun, fósil Lesululi nian la'ós dinosauru nian.
text.pt: Os pterossauros foram répteis voadores que viveram há cerca de 228 a 66 milhões de anos, no tempo dos dinossauros. Foram os primeiros animais com coluna vertebral a voar batendo as asas, muito antes das aves e dos morcegos. A asa era uma membrana de pele presa a um quarto dedo muito comprido. Tinham ossos ocos e leves. Alguns eram do tamanho de um pássaro pequeno; outros tinham cerca de 10 metros de uma ponta da asa à outra. Atenção: os pterossauros não eram dinossauros nem aves, mas parentes próximos dos dinossauros. Por isso, mesmo que a identificação se confirme, o fóssil de Lesululi não será um fóssil de dinossauro.
text.en: Pterosaurs were flying reptiles that lived about 228 to 66 million years ago, in the time of the dinosaurs. They were the first animals with a backbone to fly by flapping their wings, long before birds and bats. The wing was a membrane of skin attached to a very long fourth finger. Their bones were hollow and light. Some were the size of a small bird; others measured about 10 metres from one wingtip to the other. Take note: pterosaurs were neither dinosaurs nor birds, but close relatives of the dinosaurs. So even if the identification is confirmed, the Lesululi fossil will not be a dinosaur fossil.
text.id: Pterosaurus adalah reptil terbang yang hidup sekitar 228 sampai 66 juta tahun lalu, pada zaman dinosaurus. Hewan ini adalah hewan bertulang belakang pertama yang terbang dengan mengepakkan sayap, jauh sebelum burung dan kelelawar. Sayapnya berupa selaput kulit yang melekat pada jari keempat yang sangat panjang. Tulangnya berongga dan ringan. Ada yang sebesar burung kecil; ada pula yang rentang sayapnya sekitar 10 meter dari ujung sayap yang satu ke ujung yang lain. Perhatikan: pterosaurus bukan dinosaurus dan bukan burung, melainkan kerabat dekat dinosaurus. Karena itu, kalaupun identifikasinya terbukti, fosil Lesululi bukanlah fosil dinosaurus.

heading.pt: O monte Lesululi e os seus ictiossauros

text.tet: Foho Lesululi iha Kailaku, munisípiu Bobonaru, iha nasaun nia parte loro-monu. Iha tinan 2020, durante peskiza jeolójika ida, ekipa IGTL nian hetan iha ne'ebá iktiosauru sira-nia ruin. Fatuk sira husi Triásiku; notísia ida husi tinan 2026 dehan katak ruin sira-ne'e tuan liu tinan tokon 208, no notísia seluk dehan maizumenus tinan tokon 250. Iha tinan 2023, sientista husi Muzeu Evolusaun Universidade Uppsala nian (Suésia), Muzeu Istória Naturál Universidade Oslo nian (Noruega) no Universidade Austrália Osidentál halo serbisu-kampu hamutuk ho IGTL. Institutu ne'e serbisu mós ho BBC ba dokumentáriu ida kona-ba iktiosauru ne'e, ne'ebé sei sai iha tinan 2028. Prezidente Repúblika José Ramos-Horta vizita fatin ne'e iha Abríl 2026.
text.pt: O monte Lesululi fica em Cailaco, no município de Bobonaro, no oeste do país. Em 2020, durante um levantamento geológico, uma equipa do IGTL encontrou ali ossos de ictiossauros. As rochas são do Triásico; uma notícia de 2026 dá aos ossos mais de 208 milhões de anos, e outras falam em cerca de 250 milhões. Em 2023, cientistas do Museu da Evolução da Universidade de Uppsala (Suécia), do Museu de História Natural da Universidade de Oslo (Noruega) e da Universidade da Austrália Ocidental fizeram trabalho de campo com o IGTL. O instituto trabalha também com a BBC num documentário sobre o ictiossauro, previsto para 2028. O Presidente José Ramos-Horta visitou o local em abril de 2026.
text.en: Mount Lesululi is in Cailaco, in Bobonaro municipality, in the west of the country. In 2020, during a geological survey, an IGTL team found ichthyosaur bones there. The rocks are Triassic; a 2026 news report gives the bones an age of more than 208 million years, and others speak of about 250 million. In 2023 scientists from the Museum of Evolution of Uppsala University (Sweden), the Natural History Museum of the University of Oslo (Norway) and the University of Western Australia did fieldwork with the IGTL. The institute is also working with the BBC on a documentary about the ichthyosaur, planned for 2028. President José Ramos-Horta visited the site in April 2026.
text.id: Gunung Lesululi terletak di Cailaco, munisipalitas Bobonaro, di bagian barat negara ini. Pada 2020, saat survei geologi, tim IGTL menemukan tulang iktiosaurus di sana. Batuannya berasal dari zaman Trias; sebuah berita tahun 2026 menyebut umur tulang itu lebih dari 208 juta tahun, sedangkan berita lain menyebut sekitar 250 juta tahun. Pada 2023, ilmuwan dari Museum Evolusi Universitas Uppsala (Swedia), Museum Sejarah Alam Universitas Oslo (Norwegia), dan Universitas Australia Barat melakukan kerja lapangan bersama IGTL. Lembaga itu juga bekerja sama dengan BBC membuat film dokumenter tentang iktiosaurus tersebut, yang direncanakan pada 2028. Presiden José Ramos-Horta mengunjungi lokasi itu pada April 2026.

heading.pt: Porque é que a descoberta é importante

text.tet: Pterosauru sira-nia ruin mihis no mamuk, tan ne'e sira kotu fasil no raru mak sai fósil. Bainhira pterosauru ida mate iha tasi leten, nia isin bele tun ba tasi okos no rai-tahu taka nia, besik animál tasi nian hanesan iktiosauru. Se espesialista sira konfirma identifikasaun ne'e, Lesululi sei iha pterosauru dahuluk ne'ebé ema hatene iha Timór-Leste, kapítulu foun ida iha réptil sira-nia istória husi dinosauru sira-nia tempu. To'o ne'ebá, presiza pasiénsia: siénsia presiza kompara ruin sira ho fósil seluk, sukat fatuk sira-nia idade no publika rezultadu sira atu sientista seluk bele verifika. Fósil sira-ne'e nia idade loloos seidauk publika.
text.pt: Os ossos dos pterossauros eram finos e ocos, por isso partiam-se facilmente e raramente se conservaram como fósseis. Quando um pterossauro morria sobre o mar, o corpo podia afundar e ficar coberto de lama, ao lado de animais marinhos como os ictiossauros. Se os especialistas confirmarem a identificação, Lesululi terá o primeiro pterossauro conhecido de Timor-Leste, um novo capítulo na história dos répteis do tempo dos dinossauros. Até lá, é preciso paciência: a ciência exige comparar os ossos com outros fósseis, medir a idade das rochas e publicar os resultados para que outros cientistas os possam verificar. A idade exata destes fósseis ainda não foi publicada.
text.en: Pterosaur bones were thin and hollow, so they broke easily and were rarely preserved as fossils. When a pterosaur died over the sea, its body could sink and be covered in mud, next to sea animals such as ichthyosaurs. If specialists confirm the identification, Lesululi will have the first known pterosaur from Timor-Leste, a new chapter in the story of the reptiles of the age of dinosaurs. Until then, patience is needed: science requires comparing the bones with other fossils, measuring the age of the rocks and publishing the results so that other scientists can check them. The exact age of these fossils has not yet been published.
text.id: Tulang pterosaurus tipis dan berongga, sehingga mudah patah dan jarang terawetkan sebagai fosil. Ketika seekor pterosaurus mati di atas laut, tubuhnya bisa tenggelam dan tertutup lumpur, di samping hewan laut seperti iktiosaurus. Jika para ahli memastikan identifikasinya, Lesululi akan memiliki pterosaurus pertama yang diketahui dari Timor-Leste, sebuah babak baru dalam sejarah reptil pada zaman dinosaurus. Sampai saat itu, perlu kesabaran: ilmu pengetahuan menuntut tulang-tulang itu dibandingkan dengan fosil lain, umur batuannya diukur, dan hasilnya dipublikasikan agar ilmuwan lain dapat memeriksanya. Umur pasti fosil-fosil ini belum dipublikasikan.

text.tet: Jeosítiu mak fatin ida ne'ebé fatuk ka fósil sira konta parte importante ida husi Rai nia istória. Jeoparke mundiál UNESCO nian hamutuk jeosítiu barak iha rejiaun ida, no uza sira ba edukasaun, protesaun natureza nian no turizmu, ho komunidade sira-nia partisipasaun. Desde 2025, IGTL no Estadu prepara kandidatura foho Lesululi nian ba jeoparke, no iha Jullu 2026 institutu ne'e hatudu mós Parke Nasionál Nino Konis Santana nu'udar área ida ho poténsia. IGTL ko'alia kona-ba projetu ne'e ho Rede Global Jeoparke sira-nia prezidente, Artur Sá, no halo sorumutu informasaun ba komunidade Kailaku. Ema ne'ebé vizita foho ne'e la bele ke'e ka lori fatuk ka ruin.
text.pt: Um geossítio é um lugar onde as rochas ou os fósseis contam uma parte importante da história da Terra. Um geoparque mundial da UNESCO junta vários geossítios numa região e usa-os para a educação, a proteção da natureza e o turismo, com a participação das comunidades. Desde 2025, o IGTL e o Estado preparam a candidatura do monte Lesululi a geoparque, e em julho de 2026 o instituto apontou também o Parque Nacional Nino Konis Santana como área com potencial. O IGTL falou do projeto com o presidente da Rede Global de Geoparques, Artur Sá, e organizou sessões de informação para a comunidade de Cailaco. Quem visitar o monte não deve escavar nem levar pedras ou ossos.
text.en: A geosite is a place where rocks or fossils tell an important part of the Earth's history. A UNESCO Global Geopark brings together several geosites in one region and uses them for education, nature protection and tourism, with the participation of the communities. Since 2025 the IGTL and the State have been preparing Mount Lesululi's bid to become a geopark, and in July 2026 the institute also named Nino Konis Santana National Park as an area with potential. The IGTL discussed the project with the president of the Global Geoparks Network, Artur Sá, and organised information sessions for the community of Cailaco. Visitors to the mountain must not dig or take away stones or bones.
text.id: Situs geologi (geosite) adalah tempat batuan atau fosil menceritakan bagian penting dari sejarah Bumi. Geopark Global UNESCO menggabungkan beberapa situs geologi dalam satu wilayah dan memanfaatkannya untuk pendidikan, perlindungan alam, dan pariwisata, dengan melibatkan masyarakat. Sejak 2025, IGTL dan negara menyiapkan pencalonan Gunung Lesululi sebagai geopark, dan pada Juli 2026 lembaga itu juga menyebut Taman Nasional Nino Konis Santana sebagai kawasan yang berpotensi. IGTL membicarakan proyek ini dengan presiden Jaringan Geopark Global (Global Geoparks Network), Artur Sá, dan mengadakan sesi informasi bagi masyarakat Cailaco. Pengunjung gunung itu tidak boleh menggali atau membawa pulang batu maupun tulang.

review.notes: All Lesululi facts come from Tatoli (11 Aug 2026 reports in Tetun, Portuguese and English — seen through search summaries; the owner-requested Indonesian report could not be opened) and earlier Tatoli reports; no peer-reviewed description exists yet. Place: Mount Lesululi, Cailaco administrative post, Bobonaro. Found in July 2026 during continued work on the ichthyosaur bones; reported 11 Aug 2026; identification provisional (IGTL president Job Brites dos Santos). Samples studied in Sweden, expected back for reconstruction and museum display. The English report names researchers from Uppsala University, the University of Oslo and the BBC; the Uppsala page (14 Mar 2024) adds the University of Western Australia and 2023 fieldwork. The BBC documentary planned for 2028 concerns the ichthyosaur fossil (Tatoli, Apr 2026). The pterosaur's AGE WAS NOT GIVEN — the text says so and gives the general pterosaur range (about 228–66 Ma). The article's 'period' (Triassic, 252–201 Ma) is the age reported for the Lesululi ichthyosaurs ('over 208 million years', Tatoli Apr 2026; 'about 250 million years', another report) — change it if the pterosaur proves younger. Geopark: candidacy prepared since 2025 (Tatoli pt, 2 May 2025; id/en, March 2025); Nino Konis Santana park named as a potential area (Tatoli tet, 29 Jul 2026); talks with Global Geoparks Network president Artur Sá and a community awareness event in Cailaco (search summaries). 'First pterosaur known from Timor-Leste' follows the English headline ('possible first pterosaur fossils'). Pterosaur biology (first flying vertebrates, fourth finger, wingspans up to about 10 m, not dinosaurs) is general knowledge. Timeline: -228000000 and -66000000 are the general first and last appearance of pterosaurs (range quoted in the Tatoli article); -208000000 is the reported age of the Lesululi ichthyosaurs, not of the pterosaur. Tetun terms to check: pterosauru, iktiosauru, jeosítiu, jeoparke, ruin-kotuk (backbone), liman-fuan dahaat, Muzeu Evolusaun, serbisu-kampu, sorumutu informasaun, amostra. EN/ID (2026-11-11): English and Indonesian translated by hand from the Portuguese and checked against the Tetun; Tetun and Portuguese not changed. Timeline titles shared between articles are translated identically. The Tatoli Tetun report (tatoli.tl, 11 Aug 2026) was opened on 2026-11-11: it confirms Mount Lesululi, Cailaco administrative post, Bobonaro; found in July 2026 during continued study of the ichthyosaur with Uppsala University, the University of Oslo and the BBC; provisional identification; samples sent to Sweden for study and reconstruction, then to come back for a museum; pterosaurs 228–66 million years ago; talks with GGN president Artur Sá. It names the IGTL president 'Job Brites' (no 'dos Santos') — check the full name. The English and Indonesian Tatoli pages could not be opened (host not reachable). title.pt: Animais da Idade do Gelo: Stegodon, ratos gigantes e tartarugas-gigantes
title.en: Ice Age animals: Stegodon, giant rats and giant tortoises
title.id: Hewan Zaman Es: Stegodon, tikus raksasa, dan kura-kura raksasa

summary.tet: Molok ema to'o, Timór iha animál sira ne'ebé ohin la iha ona: elefante nia família ki'ik ida, lenuk boot no laho boot tebes. Sira to'o ho nani ka namlele, tanba tasi kle'an haleu illa ne'e nafatin. Stegodon lakon molok ema to'o; laho boot sira moris hamutuk ho ema no lakon iha tinan rihun hirak ikus ne'e.
summary.pt: Antes de as pessoas chegarem, Timor tinha animais que já não existem: um pequeno parente dos elefantes, tartarugas-gigantes e ratos enormes. Chegaram a nadar ou a flutuar, porque a ilha sempre esteve rodeada de mar profundo. O Stegodon desapareceu antes das pessoas; os ratos gigantes viveram ao lado delas e extinguiram-se nos últimos milhares de anos.
summary.en: Before people arrived, Timor had animals that no longer exist: a small relative of elephants, giant tortoises and enormous rats. They got there by swimming or floating, because the island has always been surrounded by deep sea. Stegodon disappeared before people came; the giant rats lived alongside people and died out in the last few thousand years.
summary.id: Sebelum manusia datang, Timor memiliki hewan-hewan yang kini sudah tidak ada: kerabat kecil gajah, kura-kura raksasa, dan tikus yang sangat besar. Hewan-hewan itu sampai ke sana dengan berenang atau mengapung, karena pulau ini selalu dikelilingi laut dalam. Stegodon punah sebelum manusia datang; tikus raksasa hidup berdampingan dengan manusia dan punah dalam beberapa ribu tahun terakhir.

text.tet: Tempu jelu, ka Pleistosénu, hahú maizumenus tinan tokon 2,6 liubá no remata maizumenus tinan 11 700 liubá. Iha tempu ne'e tasi nia nível tun dala barak, maibé Timór nunka liga ho Ázia ka Austrália liuhusi rai-maran. Tan ne'e, animál sira ne'ebé bele nani, semo ka namlele hamutuk ho ai-kain no ai-horis ne'ebé tasi lori de'it mak to'o illa ne'e. Elefante sira nani di'ak, no laho no lenuk bele moris loron barak iha tasi leten. Iha illa sira, animál sira muda: dala barak animál boot sai ki'ik, tanba hahán la barak, no animál ki'ik bele sai boot, tanba animál ne'ebé han sira la barak. Sientista sira bolu ida-ne'e 'regra illa nian'.
text.pt: A Idade do Gelo, ou Plistocénico, durou de há cerca de 2,6 milhões de anos até há uns 11 700 anos. Nesse tempo, o nível do mar desceu muitas vezes, mas Timor nunca ficou ligada por terra à Ásia nem à Austrália. Só chegaram, por isso, animais que sabiam nadar, voar ou viajar agarrados a troncos e plantas levados pelo mar. Os elefantes nadam bem, e os ratos e as tartarugas podem sobreviver dias a flutuar. Nas ilhas, os animais mudam: os grandes ficam muitas vezes mais pequenos, porque há pouca comida, e os pequenos podem ficar grandes, porque há poucos predadores. Os cientistas chamam a isto a «regra das ilhas».
text.en: The Ice Age, or Pleistocene, lasted from about 2.6 million years ago until about 11,700 years ago. During that time the sea level fell many times, but Timor was never joined by land to Asia or Australia. So the only animals that arrived were those that could swim, fly or travel clinging to logs and plants carried by the sea. Elephants are good swimmers, and rats and tortoises can survive for days while floating. On islands, animals change: large ones often become smaller, because there is little food, and small ones can become large, because there are few predators. Scientists call this the 'island rule'.
text.id: Zaman Es, atau Pleistosen, berlangsung dari sekitar 2,6 juta tahun lalu hingga sekitar 11.700 tahun lalu. Pada masa itu, permukaan laut turun berkali-kali, tetapi Timor tidak pernah tersambung lewat daratan dengan Asia maupun Australia. Karena itu, yang sampai ke pulau ini hanya hewan yang bisa berenang, terbang, atau terbawa sambil berpegangan pada batang kayu dan tumbuhan yang hanyut di laut. Gajah pandai berenang, sedangkan tikus dan kura-kura dapat bertahan berhari-hari sambil mengapung. Di pulau, hewan berubah: hewan besar sering menjadi lebih kecil karena makanannya sedikit, dan hewan kecil bisa menjadi besar karena pemangsanya sedikit. Ilmuwan menyebut hal ini 'aturan pulau'.

text.tet: Stegodon mak elefante nia família, ho nehan-naruk sira no nehan boot sira atu han ai-horis. Espésie Timór nian, Stegodon timorensis, sientista Indonézia Sartono mak deskreve iha tinan 1969, husi nehan molár ida ne'ebé la kompletu, no animál ne'e ki'ik liu stegodon sira iha kontinente. Iha tinan 2016, sientista Louys, Price no O'Connor sukat ba dala uluk stegodon Timór nian nia nehan-naruk ida nia idade. Sira hetan nehan-naruk ne'e iha Timór loro-monu, iha fatuk-oan nia kamada sira naran Ainaro Gravels, no nia idade tinan 130 000 ka liu. Ida-ne'e uluk liu ema to'o. Peskizadór sira hanoin katak stegodon Timór nian karik lakon tanba populasaun ki'ik ida ne'ebé mesak tun neineik.
text.pt: O Stegodon era parente dos elefantes, com presas compridas e dentes grandes para comer plantas. A espécie de Timor, Stegodon timorensis, foi descrita em 1969 pelo cientista indonésio Sartono, a partir de um dente molar incompleto, e era bem mais pequena do que os stegodons do continente. Em 2016, os cientistas Louys, Price e O'Connor dataram pela primeira vez uma presa de stegodon de Timor, encontrada em Timor Ocidental, em camadas de cascalho chamadas Ainaro Gravels: tinha 130 000 anos ou mais. Isto é muito antes da chegada das pessoas. Os autores pensam que o stegodon de Timor pode ter desaparecido pelo declínio lento de uma população pequena e isolada.
text.en: Stegodon was a relative of elephants, with long tusks and large teeth for eating plants. The Timor species, Stegodon timorensis, was described in 1969 by the Indonesian scientist Sartono from an incomplete molar tooth, and it was much smaller than the stegodons of the mainland. In 2016 the scientists Louys, Price and O'Connor dated a stegodon tusk from Timor for the first time; it had been found in West Timor, in layers of gravel called the Ainaro Gravels, and was 130,000 years old or more. This is long before people arrived. The authors think that the Timor stegodon may have disappeared through the slow decline of a small, isolated population.
text.id: Stegodon adalah kerabat gajah, dengan gading panjang dan gigi besar untuk memakan tumbuhan. Spesies Timor, Stegodon timorensis, dideskripsikan pada 1969 oleh ilmuwan Indonesia Sartono berdasarkan sebuah gigi geraham yang tidak lengkap, dan ukurannya jauh lebih kecil daripada stegodon di daratan besar. Pada 2016, ilmuwan Louys, Price, dan O'Connor untuk pertama kalinya menentukan umur sebuah gading stegodon dari Timor, yang ditemukan di Timor Barat, di lapisan kerikil yang disebut Ainaro Gravels: umurnya 130.000 tahun atau lebih. Ini jauh sebelum manusia datang. Para penulisnya menduga stegodon Timor mungkin punah karena penurunan perlahan sebuah populasi yang kecil dan terisolasi.

text.tet: Timór mós iha lenuk boot sira ne'ebé hela iha rai-maran, husi grupu Megalochelys, família ho lenuk sira ne'ebé uluk moris iha Ázia kontinente, Java no Flores. Paleontólogu olandés Dirk Hooijer deskreve sira-nia fósil iha tinan 1971. Fósil sira hatudu katak lenuk sira-ne'e hela iha illa ne'e iha Pleistosénu Médiu no Superiór, maizumenus entre tinan 800 000 no 120 000 liubá, no lenuk Timór nian karik espésie mesak ida. Iha mós relatóriu kona-ba lagartu boot ida nia ruin, família ho dragaun Komodo. Ohin loron, réptil boot liu iha Timór mak lafaek, no lagartu varanu sira ne'ebé hela iha ne'e ki'ik, hanesan varanu Timór.
text.pt: Timor teve também tartarugas-gigantes terrestres do grupo Megalochelys, parentes de tartarugas que viveram no continente asiático, em Java e nas Flores. Os seus fósseis foram descritos em 1971 pelo paleontólogo holandês Dirk Hooijer. Mostram que estas tartarugas viveram na ilha no Plistocénico Médio e Superior, mais ou menos entre 800 000 e 120 000 anos atrás, e a forma de Timor pode ter sido uma espécie própria. Há ainda relatos de ossos de um grande lagarto-monitor, parente do dragão-de-komodo. Hoje, o maior réptil de Timor é o crocodilo-de-água-salgada, e os varanos que lá vivem são pequenos, como o varano-de-timor.
text.en: Timor also had giant land tortoises of the group Megalochelys, relatives of tortoises that lived on the Asian mainland, in Java and on Flores. Their fossils were described in 1971 by the Dutch palaeontologist Dirk Hooijer. They show that these tortoises lived on the island in the Middle and Late Pleistocene, roughly between 800,000 and 120,000 years ago, and the Timor form may have been a species of its own. There are also reports of bones of a large monitor lizard, a relative of the Komodo dragon. Today the largest reptile on Timor is the saltwater crocodile, and the monitor lizards that live there are small, such as the Timor monitor.
text.id: Timor juga pernah memiliki kura-kura darat raksasa dari kelompok Megalochelys, kerabat kura-kura yang hidup di daratan Asia, di Jawa, dan di Flores. Fosilnya dideskripsikan pada 1971 oleh paleontolog Belanda Dirk Hooijer. Fosil itu menunjukkan bahwa kura-kura ini hidup di pulau ini pada Pleistosen Tengah dan Akhir, kira-kira antara 800.000 dan 120.000 tahun lalu, dan bentuk dari Timor mungkin merupakan spesies tersendiri. Ada pula laporan tentang tulang biawak besar, kerabat komodo. Kini reptil terbesar di Timor adalah buaya muara, dan biawak yang hidup di sana berukuran kecil, seperti biawak timor.

text.tet: Laho boot sira Timór nian parte husi jéneru Coryphomys. Espésie dahuluk, Coryphomys buehleri, sientista sira deskreve iha tinan 1937 husi ruin sira husi fatuk-kuak ida besik Nikiniki, iha Timór loro-monu. Iha tinan 2010, zoólogu Ken Aplin no Kristofer Helgen deskreve espésie daruak ida, Coryphomys musseri, ho ruin sira ne'ebé ema ke'e iha fatuk-kuak sira Timór-Leste nian. Sira-ne'ebé boot liu bele todan maizumenus kg 5, hanesan asu ki'ik, maski estimativa sira la hanesan. Sira moris hamutuk ho laho espésie seluk ne'ebé iha de'it iha Timór. Sira-nia ruin mosu iha fatuk-kuak nia kamada sira ne'ebé ema uza, besik hahán nia rastu, tan ne'e karik ema mós kasa sira.
text.pt: Os ratos gigantes de Timor pertenciam ao género Coryphomys. A primeira espécie, Coryphomys buehleri, foi descrita em 1937 a partir de ossos de uma gruta perto de Nikiniki, em Timor Ocidental. Em 2010, os zoólogos Ken Aplin e Kristofer Helgen descreveram uma segunda espécie, Coryphomys musseri, com ossos escavados em grutas de Timor-Leste. Os maiores podiam pesar cerca de 5 kg, como um cão pequeno, embora as estimativas variem. Viviam ao lado de outras espécies de ratos que só existiam em Timor. Os seus ossos aparecem nas camadas das grutas usadas por pessoas, junto a restos de comida, por isso é provável que também fossem caçados.
text.en: Timor's giant rats belonged to the genus Coryphomys. The first species, Coryphomys buehleri, was described in 1937 from bones found in a cave near Nikiniki, in West Timor. In 2010 the zoologists Ken Aplin and Kristofer Helgen described a second species, Coryphomys musseri, from bones excavated in caves in Timor-Leste. The largest could weigh about 5 kg, like a small dog, although estimates vary. They lived alongside other species of rats found only on Timor. Their bones appear in the layers of caves used by people, next to food remains, so they were probably hunted too.
text.id: Tikus raksasa Timor termasuk genus Coryphomys. Spesies pertama, Coryphomys buehleri, dideskripsikan pada 1937 berdasarkan tulang dari sebuah gua di dekat Nikiniki, Timor Barat. Pada 2010, ahli zoologi Ken Aplin dan Kristofer Helgen mendeskripsikan spesies kedua, Coryphomys musseri, dari tulang yang digali di gua-gua Timor-Leste. Yang terbesar bisa mencapai berat sekitar 5 kg, seperti anjing kecil, meskipun perkiraannya berbeda-beda. Tikus ini hidup berdampingan dengan spesies tikus lain yang hanya ada di Timor. Tulangnya muncul di lapisan gua yang dipakai manusia, di dekat sisa makanan, sehingga kemungkinan besar tikus ini juga diburu.

text.tet: Estuda lakon sira-ne'e ajuda atu proteje animál ohin loron nian. Iha Timór, Stegodon lakon uluk liu ema to'o. Ho laho boot sira, istória la hanesan. Estudu ida husi tinan 2023, husi Louys, O'Connor no kolega sira, hatudu katak durante tinan liu 40 000 ne'ebé ema hela iha Timór, kuaze la iha animál ida mak lakon. Laho endémiku barak liu lakon de'it iha tinan rihun hirak ikus ne'e, karik entre tinan 2 000 no 1 000 liubá. Kauza prinsipál mak katak illa ne'e nia ai-laran orijinál kuaze lakon hotu, tanba ema ko'a atu halo to'os no knua. Dadus sira seidauk hatudu katak animál ne'ebé ema lori mai to'o iha tempu hanesan ho lakon sira-ne'e.
text.pt: Estudar estas extinções ajuda a proteger os animais de hoje. Em Timor, o Stegodon desapareceu muito antes de haver pessoas. Com os ratos gigantes foi diferente. Um estudo de 2023, de Louys, O'Connor e colegas, mostra que, durante mais de 40 000 anos de presença humana, quase não houve extinções. A maior parte dos ratos endémicos desapareceu só nos últimos milhares de anos, provavelmente entre há 2000 e 1000 anos. A causa principal parece ter sido a perda quase total das florestas originais da ilha, cortadas para campos e aldeias. Os dados ainda não mostram que a chegada dos animais trazidos pelas pessoas coincida com estas extinções.
text.en: Studying these extinctions helps to protect the animals of today. On Timor, Stegodon disappeared long before there were people. With the giant rats it was different. A 2023 study by Louys, O'Connor and colleagues shows that during more than 40,000 years of human presence there were almost no extinctions. Most of the endemic rats disappeared only in the last few thousand years, probably between 2,000 and 1,000 years ago. The main cause seems to have been the almost total loss of the island's original forests, cut down for fields and villages. The data do not yet show that the arrival of animals brought by people coincided with these extinctions.
text.id: Mempelajari kepunahan ini membantu melindungi hewan masa kini. Di Timor, Stegodon punah jauh sebelum ada manusia. Tikus raksasa mengalami hal yang berbeda. Penelitian tahun 2023 oleh Louys, O'Connor, dan rekan-rekannya menunjukkan bahwa selama lebih dari 40.000 tahun kehadiran manusia, hampir tidak terjadi kepunahan. Sebagian besar tikus endemik baru punah dalam beberapa ribu tahun terakhir, kemungkinan antara 2.000 dan 1.000 tahun lalu. Penyebab utamanya tampaknya adalah hilangnya hampir seluruh hutan asli pulau ini, yang ditebang untuk ladang dan kampung. Data yang ada belum menunjukkan bahwa kedatangan hewan yang dibawa manusia terjadi bersamaan dengan kepunahan ini.

The find spot is given as West Timor because the paper is titled 'Timor Island, East Nusa Tenggara' — check. Extinction by slow demographic and genetic decline is the authors' suggestion. Hooijer's first name (Dirk) from general knowledge. KOMODO-LIKE MONITOR ON TIMOR: not confirmed by my searches — from general knowledge (Hocknull et al. 2009, PLoS ONE, 'Dragon's Paradise Lost'); check or delete that sentence. Coryphomys: C. buehleri described 1937 (Schaub) from a cave near Nikiniki, West Timor; C. musseri Aplin & Helgen 2010 from East Timor archaeological deposits; about 5 kg (estimates vary; 6 kg is uncited); extinct roughly 2,000–1,000 years ago (Wikipedia). Louys et al. 2023 (Records of the Australian Museum 75(5)): few if any extinctions in 40,000+ years until the last few thousand; forest loss the main driver; no dated overlap with introductions (source title written descriptively). 'Bones next to food remains, so probably hunted' is an inference — check. Pleistocene 2.6 Ma–11,700 years and the island rule are general knowledge. Quiz 3 Tetun option uses 'grama' — check spelling. title.tet: Liu tasi: oinsá ema dahuluk to'o Timór
title.pt: Atravessar o mar: como os primeiros povos chegaram a Timor
title.en: Crossing the sea: how the first peoples reached Timor
title.id: Menyeberangi laut: bagaimana manusia pertama sampai ke Timor

summary.tet: Timór nunka liga ho kontinente ida liuhusi rai-maran, maski iha tempu jelu. Tan ne'e, ema dahuluk, ne'ebé to'o maizumenus tinan 44 000 liubá, tenke liu tasi ho rakit ka ró. Sira mós peskadór matenek: iha Jerimalai sira kaer atun maizumenus tinan 42 000 liubá.
summary.pt: Timor nunca esteve ligada por terra a nenhum continente, nem mesmo na Idade do Gelo. Por isso, as primeiras pessoas, que chegaram há cerca de 44 000 anos, tiveram de atravessar o mar em jangadas ou barcos. Eram também grandes pescadores: em Jerimalai apanhavam atum há cerca de 42 000 anos.
summary.en: Timor was never joined by land to any continent, not even in the Ice Age. So the first people, who arrived about 44,000 years ago, had to cross the sea on rafts or in boats. They were also great fishers: at Jerimalai they were catching tuna about 42,000 years ago.
summary.id: Timor tidak pernah tersambung lewat daratan dengan benua mana pun, bahkan pada Zaman Es. Karena itu, manusia pertama, yang tiba sekitar 44.000 tahun lalu, harus menyeberangi laut dengan rakit atau perahu. Mereka juga nelayan yang hebat: di Jerimalai mereka sudah menangkap tuna sekitar 42.000 tahun lalu.

heading.tet: Kontinente maran rua no tasi ida ho illa barak
heading.pt: Dois continentes secos e um mar de ilhas
heading.en: Two dry continents and a sea of islands
heading.id: Dua benua kering dan lautan pulau

text.tet: Iha tempu jelu, bee barak hela iha jelu boot sira, no tasi nia nível tun. Iha tempu ne'ebé malirin liu, maizumenus tinan 21 000 liubá, tasi nia nível tun maizumenus metru 120 kompara ho ohin. Iha tempu ne'ebá, Sumatra, Java no Bornéu sai rai boot ida ne'ebé liga ho Ázia, naran Sunda. Austrália, Nova Giné no Tasmánia sai rai boot seluk, naran Sahul. Entre rai rua ne'e iha Wallacea, tasi ida ho illa barak ne'ebé haketak malu ho estreitu kle'an tebes, ne'ebé nunka maran. Timór mak illa ida husi sira. Zona ne'e iha naran husi naturalista Alfred Russel Wallace, ne'ebé estuda illa sira-ne'e nia animál iha sékulu 19.
text.pt: Na Idade do Gelo, muita água ficou presa em enormes glaciares e o nível do mar desceu. No momento mais frio, há cerca de 21 000 anos, estava uns 120 metros abaixo do atual. Sumatra, Java e Bornéu formavam então uma grande terra ligada à Ásia, chamada Sunda. A Austrália, a Nova Guiné e a Tasmânia formavam outra, chamada Sahul. Entre as duas ficava a Wallacea, um mar cheio de ilhas separadas por estreitos tão fundos que nunca secaram. Timor é uma delas. A zona tem o nome do naturalista Alfred Russel Wallace, que estudou os animais destas ilhas no século XIX.
text.en: In the Ice Age, a great deal of water was locked up in huge glaciers and the sea level fell. At the coldest point, about 21,000 years ago, it was some 120 metres below today's level. Sumatra, Java and Borneo then formed one large landmass joined to Asia, called Sunda. Australia, New Guinea and Tasmania formed another, called Sahul. Between the two lay Wallacea, a sea full of islands separated by straits so deep that they never dried out. Timor is one of these islands. The area is named after the naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace, who studied the animals of these islands in the 19th century.
text.id: Pada Zaman Es, banyak air terperangkap dalam gletser raksasa dan permukaan laut turun. Pada masa terdingin, sekitar 21.000 tahun lalu, permukaan laut sekitar 120 meter lebih rendah daripada sekarang. Sumatra, Jawa, dan Kalimantan saat itu membentuk satu daratan besar yang tersambung dengan Asia, yang disebut Sunda. Australia, Nugini, dan Tasmania membentuk daratan lain yang disebut Sahul. Di antara keduanya terdapat Wallacea, laut yang penuh pulau yang dipisahkan oleh selat-selat yang begitu dalam sehingga tidak pernah kering. Timor adalah salah satu pulau itu. Kawasan ini dinamai menurut naturalis Alfred Russel Wallace, yang mempelajari hewan-hewan di pulau-pulau ini pada abad ke-19.

heading.tet: Viajen ida ne'ebé tenke liu tasi
heading.pt: Uma viagem que obrigava a atravessar o mar
heading.en: A journey that meant crossing the sea

text.tet: Atu bá husi Sunda ba Sahul, ema tenke liu tasi dala barak. Maski nune'e, ema hela ona iha Austrália tinan 50 000 liubá ka uluk liu, no estudu balu dehan tinan 65 000. Molok sira, ema espésie seluk to'o ona illa balu iha Wallacea: iha Flores moris Homo floresiensis ne'ebé ki'ik, no ninia bei'ala sira to'o ne'ebá maizumenus tinan tokon ida liubá. Maibé iha Timór seidauk iha prova klaru kona-ba ema tuan sira-ne'e. Rastu tuan liu iha Timór mai husi ema hanesan ita, Homo sapiens, iha fatuk-kuak Laili, maizumenus tinan 44 000 liubá. Ekipa Laili nian hanoin katak ema dahuluk ne'ebé to'o Austrália, uluk liu, karik la liu Timór.
text.pt: Para ir de Sunda para Sahul era obrigatório atravessar vários braços de mar. Mesmo assim, há pelo menos 50 000 anos já havia pessoas na Austrália, e alguns estudos apontam para 65 000 anos. Antes delas, outros humanos já tinham chegado a ilhas da Wallacea: nas Flores viveu o pequeno Homo floresiensis, cujos antepassados lá chegaram há cerca de um milhão de anos. Em Timor, porém, ainda não há provas claras desses humanos antigos. Os vestígios mais antigos da ilha são de pessoas como nós, Homo sapiens, no abrigo de Laili, há cerca de 44 000 anos. A equipa de Laili pensa que os primeiros a chegar à Austrália, mais cedo, provavelmente não passaram por Timor.
text.en: To get from Sunda to Sahul, people had to cross several stretches of sea. Even so, there were people in Australia at least 50,000 years ago, and some studies point to 65,000 years. Before them, other humans had already reached islands of Wallacea: the small Homo floresiensis lived on Flores, and its ancestors got there about a million years ago. On Timor, however, there is still no clear evidence of these ancient humans. The oldest traces on the island are of people like us, Homo sapiens, at the Laili rock shelter, about 44,000 years ago. The Laili team thinks that the first people to reach Australia, earlier, probably did not pass through Timor.
text.id: Untuk pergi dari Sunda ke Sahul, orang harus menyeberangi beberapa bentangan laut. Meski begitu, sedikitnya 50.000 tahun lalu sudah ada manusia di Australia, dan sebagian penelitian menyebut 65.000 tahun. Sebelum mereka, manusia jenis lain sudah sampai ke pulau-pulau di Wallacea: di Flores hidup Homo floresiensis yang bertubuh kecil, yang leluhurnya tiba di sana sekitar satu juta tahun lalu. Namun, di Timor belum ada bukti yang jelas tentang manusia purba itu. Jejak tertua di pulau ini berasal dari manusia seperti kita, Homo sapiens, di ceruk batu Laili, sekitar 44.000 tahun lalu. Tim Laili menduga bahwa orang-orang pertama yang tiba di Australia, lebih awal, kemungkinan besar tidak melewati Timor.

text.tet: La iha ró ida husi tempu ne'ebá ne'ebé to'o ohin: ai, au no tali sira dodok. Arkeólogu sira hanoin katak ema uza rakit husi au ka bero simples. Iha loron ne'ebé lalehan moos, illa barak iha Wallacea bele haree malu, no ahi-suar husi ahi ne'ebé han ai-laran iha illa viziñu bele hatudu katak iha rai iha sorin seluk. Ema la to'o de'it tanba aksidente, hanesan peskadór ne'ebé anin-boot lori lakon. Iha Laili, ema nia rastu mosu derepente no barak tebes, no ida-ne'e hatudu katak grupu boot ida to'o hamutuk. Viajen hanesan ne'e presiza planu, hahán no bee ba dalan, no matenek kona-ba tasi nia korrente no anin.
text.pt: Nenhum barco desse tempo chegou até nós: a madeira, o bambu e as cordas apodrecem. Os arqueólogos pensam que as pessoas usavam jangadas de bambu ou canoas simples. Em dias limpos, muitas ilhas da Wallacea veem-se umas das outras, e o fumo dos incêndios nas ilhas vizinhas podia mostrar que havia terra do outro lado. As travessias não foram só acidentes de pescadores arrastados por tempestades. Em Laili, os vestígios aparecem de repente e em grande quantidade, o que sugere a chegada de um grupo numeroso. Uma viagem assim exigia planeamento, comida e água para o caminho, e conhecimento das correntes e dos ventos.
text.en: No boat from that time has survived: wood, bamboo and rope rot away. Archaeologists think that people used bamboo rafts or simple canoes. On clear days, many islands of Wallacea can be seen from one another, and smoke from fires on neighbouring islands could show that there was land on the other side. The crossings were not just accidents of fishers swept away by storms. At Laili, the traces appear suddenly and in large numbers, which suggests the arrival of a large group. A journey like this needed planning, food and water for the way, and knowledge of currents and winds.
text.id: Tidak ada perahu dari masa itu yang bertahan sampai sekarang: kayu, bambu, dan tali membusuk. Para arkeolog menduga orang memakai rakit bambu atau perahu sederhana. Pada hari yang cerah, banyak pulau di Wallacea dapat saling terlihat, dan asap kebakaran di pulau tetangga bisa menunjukkan bahwa ada daratan di seberang. Penyeberangan itu bukan sekadar kecelakaan nelayan yang terseret badai. Di Laili, jejak manusia muncul tiba-tiba dan dalam jumlah besar, yang menunjukkan kedatangan sebuah kelompok besar. Perjalanan seperti itu membutuhkan perencanaan, makanan dan air untuk di jalan, serta pengetahuan tentang arus dan angin.

text.tet: Ema ne'ebé liu tasi to'o Timór hatene tasi di'ak. Iha fatuk-kuak Jerimalai, besik Tutuala, iha ikan nia ruin ho idade maizumenus tinan 42 000, no maizumenus metade mai husi ikan tasi kle'an nian, hanesan atun. Ida-ne'e prova tuan liu ida iha mundu kona-ba kaer ikan iha tasi kle'an. Atu kaer ikan lalais sira-ne'e, ema tenke sai ho ró, hatene tempu sira no uza kail ka redi. Depois, maizumenus tinan 23 000 to'o 16 000 liubá, peskadór Jerimalai nian halo anzól husi kulit-tasi, ida husi anzól tuan liu ne'ebé ema hatene. Deskobrimentu sira-ne'e hatudu katak, husi hahú kedas, la'o-tasi no kaer ikan mak parte husi moris iha Timór.
text.pt: As pessoas que atravessaram para Timor conheciam bem o mar. No abrigo de Jerimalai, perto de Tutuala, há ossos de peixe com cerca de 42 000 anos, e cerca de metade são de peixes de alto mar, como o atum. É uma das provas mais antigas do mundo de pesca em mar profundo. Para apanhar estes peixes rápidos era preciso sair de barco, conhecer as estações e usar linhas ou redes. Mais tarde, há cerca de 23 000 a 16 000 anos, os pescadores de Jerimalai faziam anzóis de concha, dos mais antigos que se conhecem. Estas descobertas mostram que, desde o início, navegar e pescar fizeram parte da vida em Timor.
text.en: The people who crossed to Timor knew the sea well. At the Jerimalai rock shelter, near Tutuala, there are fish bones about 42,000 years old, and about half of them come from open-sea fish such as tuna. This is some of the oldest evidence in the world of deep-sea fishing. To catch these fast fish, people had to go out in boats, know the seasons and use lines or nets. Later, about 23,000 to 16,000 years ago, the fishers of Jerimalai made fish hooks from shell, among the oldest known. These discoveries show that, from the very beginning, sailing and fishing were part of life on Timor.
text.id: Orang-orang yang menyeberang ke Timor sangat mengenal laut. Di ceruk batu Jerimalai, dekat Tutuala, terdapat tulang ikan berumur sekitar 42.000 tahun, dan sekitar separuhnya berasal dari ikan laut lepas seperti tuna. Ini salah satu bukti tertua di dunia tentang penangkapan ikan di laut dalam. Untuk menangkap ikan-ikan yang cepat ini, orang harus melaut dengan perahu, mengenal musim, dan memakai tali pancing atau jaring. Kemudian, sekitar 23.000 sampai 16.000 tahun lalu, para nelayan Jerimalai membuat kail dari cangkang kerang, termasuk yang tertua yang diketahui. Penemuan ini menunjukkan bahwa sejak awal, berlayar dan menangkap ikan sudah menjadi bagian dari kehidupan di Timor.

heading.tet: Dalan illa sira nian, bá no fila
heading.pt: Um caminho de ilhas, de ida e volta
heading.en: A path of islands, there and back

text.tet: Sientista sira diskute dalan ne'ebé viajante dahuluk sira liu entre Sunda no Sahul. Dalan norte nian liu Selebes (Sulawesi) no Maluku to'o Nova Giné; dalan sul nian liu Timór to'o Austrália. Dadus husi Laili hatudu katak ema dahuluk ne'ebé to'o Austrália karik liu dalan seluk, karik dalan norte, maibé ema to'o Timór tinan rihun balu depois, no viajen entre illa sira kontinua. Bainhira tempu jelu remata, maizumenus tinan 11 700 liubá, tasi sa'e durante tinan rihun barak no taka tasi-ibun tuan sira, hamutuk ho fatin arkeolójiku barak. Tinan rihun barak depois, ró-na'in seluk to'o: Austronézia sira, ho bero foun no ai-horis foun.
text.pt: Os cientistas discutem por onde passaram os primeiros viajantes entre Sunda e Sahul. Um caminho do norte iria por Celebes (Sulawesi) e pelas Molucas até à Nova Guiné; um caminho do sul passaria por Timor até à Austrália. Os dados de Laili sugerem que os primeiros a chegar à Austrália seguiram outro caminho, talvez o do norte, mas Timor foi povoada alguns milhares de anos mais tarde, e as viagens entre ilhas continuaram. Quando a Idade do Gelo acabou, há cerca de 11 700 anos, o mar subiu durante milhares de anos e cobriu as antigas costas, com muitos sítios arqueológicos. Milhares de anos depois chegaram outros navegadores, os austronésios, com novas canoas e novas plantas.
text.en: Scientists debate which way the first travellers went between Sunda and Sahul. A northern route would have gone through Celebes (Sulawesi) and the Moluccas to New Guinea; a southern route would have passed through Timor to Australia. The Laili data suggest that the first people to reach Australia took another route, perhaps the northern one, but Timor was settled a few thousand years later, and travel between the islands continued. When the Ice Age ended, about 11,700 years ago, the sea rose for thousands of years and covered the old coastlines, along with many archaeological sites. Thousands of years later other seafarers arrived, the Austronesians, with new canoes and new plants.
text.id: Para ilmuwan memperdebatkan jalur yang dilalui para pengembara pertama antara Sunda dan Sahul. Jalur utara akan melewati Sulawesi (Celebes) dan Maluku menuju Nugini; jalur selatan akan melewati Timor menuju Australia. Data dari Laili menunjukkan bahwa orang-orang pertama yang tiba di Australia menempuh jalur lain, mungkin jalur utara, tetapi Timor dihuni beberapa ribu tahun kemudian, dan perjalanan antarpulau terus berlanjut. Ketika Zaman Es berakhir, sekitar 11.700 tahun lalu, laut naik selama ribuan tahun dan menutupi garis pantai lama, beserta banyak situs arkeologi. Ribuan tahun kemudian datang pelaut-pelaut lain, yaitu bangsa Austronesia, dengan perahu baru dan tanaman baru.
