title.tet: Fatuk-kuak arkeolójiku sira: Jerimalai, Laili, Lene Hara no Matja Kuru
title.pt: Grutas arqueológicas: Jerimalai, Laili, Lene Hara e Matja Kuru
title.en: Archaeological caves: Jerimalai, Laili, Lene Hara and Matja Kuru
title.id: Gua-gua arkeologi: Jerimalai, Laili, Lene Hara, dan Matja Kuru

summary.tet: Fatuk-kuak sira husi fatuk-ahu iha Timór-Leste rai ema nia istória husi maizumenus tinan 44 000 liubá. Iha Laili, Jerimalai, Lene Hara, Matja Kuru no fatuk-kuak sira iha Baukau, arkeólogu sira hetan ekipamentu fatuk, ruin, kulit-tasi no sanan-rai, kamada ida iha seluk nia leten. Fatuk-kuak barak mós lulik ba komunidade sira.
summary.pt: As grutas e os abrigos de calcário de Timor-Leste guardam a história das pessoas desde há cerca de 44 000 anos. Em Laili, Jerimalai, Lene Hara, Matja Kuru e nas grutas de Baucau, os arqueólogos encontraram ferramentas de pedra, ossos, conchas e cerâmica, camada sobre camada. Muitas destas grutas são também lugares sagrados para as comunidades.
summary.en: The limestone caves and rock shelters of Timor-Leste hold the story of people going back about 44,000 years. At Laili, Jerimalai, Lene Hara, Matja Kuru and in the caves of Baucau, archaeologists have found stone tools, bones, shells and pottery, layer upon layer. Many of these caves are also sacred places for the communities.
summary.id: Gua dan ceruk batu kapur di Timor-Leste menyimpan sejarah manusia sejak sekitar 44.000 tahun lalu. Di Laili, Jerimalai, Lene Hara, Matja Kuru, dan gua-gua di Baucau, arkeolog menemukan alat batu, tulang, cangkang kerang, dan tembikar, lapis demi lapis. Banyak gua ini juga merupakan tempat sakral bagi masyarakat.

text.tet: Abrigu fatuk mak fatuk-didin ida ho fatuk ne'ebé sai ba li'ur no proteje husi udan; fatuk-kuak tama kle'an liu ba foho laran. Durante tinan rihun barak, rai, ahi nia rastu, kulit-tasi no ruin halibur iha fatin sira-ne'e nia rai, no halo kamada sira: sira-ne'ebé iha okos mak tuan liu. Arkeólogu sira ke'e neineik, kamada ida-idak, no fakar rai iha peneira atu la lakon sasán ki'ik sira. Depois sira sukat idade. Karbonu-14 bele sukat karvaun, kulit-tasi no ruin to'o maizumenus tinan 50 000. Luminesénsia hatudu bainhira rai-henek nia fuan sira hetan loron nia naroman ikus liu, no urániu sukat kamada minerál sira. Ho métodu sira-ne'e hamutuk, ema hatene bainhira ema uza fatin ida-idak.
text.pt: Um abrigo rochoso é uma parede de rocha com uma saliência que protege da chuva; uma gruta entra mais fundo na montanha. Durante milhares de anos, terra, cinzas, conchas e ossos acumularam-se no chão destes lugares e formaram camadas: as de baixo são as mais antigas. Os arqueólogos escavam devagar, camada a camada, e peneiram a terra para não perder pequenos objetos. Depois medem as idades. O carbono-14 data carvão, conchas e ossos até cerca de 50 000 anos. A luminescência mostra quando os grãos de areia viram a luz do sol pela última vez, e o urânio data crostas minerais. Juntando estes métodos, sabe-se quando as pessoas usaram cada lugar.
text.en: A rock shelter is a rock wall with an overhang that gives protection from the rain; a cave goes deeper into the hillside. Over thousands of years, soil, ash, shells and bones built up on the floor of these places and formed layers: the lowest ones are the oldest. Archaeologists dig slowly, layer by layer, and sieve the soil so as not to lose small objects. Then they measure the ages. Carbon-14 dates charcoal, shells and bones up to about 50,000 years old. Luminescence shows when grains of sand last saw sunlight, and uranium dates mineral crusts. By combining these methods, we can tell when people used each place.
text.id: Ceruk batu adalah dinding batu dengan bagian yang menjorok sehingga melindungi dari hujan; gua masuk lebih dalam ke perut bukit. Selama ribuan tahun, tanah, abu, cangkang kerang, dan tulang menumpuk di lantai tempat-tempat ini dan membentuk lapisan: lapisan paling bawah adalah yang tertua. Arkeolog menggali perlahan, lapis demi lapis, dan mengayak tanah agar benda-benda kecil tidak hilang. Kemudian mereka mengukur umurnya. Karbon-14 dapat menentukan umur arang, cangkang, dan tulang hingga sekitar 50.000 tahun. Luminesensi menunjukkan kapan butir pasir terakhir kali terkena sinar matahari, dan uranium menentukan umur kerak mineral. Dengan menggabungkan metode-metode ini, dapat diketahui kapan manusia memakai setiap tempat.

heading.tet: Laili no Jerimalai: data tuan liu sira
heading.pt: Laili e Jerimalai: as datas mais antigas
heading.en: Laili and Jerimalai: the oldest dates

text.tet: Laili mak abrigu fatuk ida iha Manatutu, iha nasaun nia parte norte. Ninia kamada tuan liu ho ema nia rastu iha idade maizumenus tinan 44 000, no iha sira-nia okos iha kamada ne'ebé la iha ema nia sinál. Ida-ne'e ajuda atu hatene loloos bainhira ema to'o. Ema iha Laili han kulit-tasi nia na'an, ikan no animál rai-maran nian, hanesan laho. Jerimalai mak abrigu fatuk ida husi fatuk-ahu besik Tutuala, iha rohan loro-sa'e. Ekipa husi Universidade Nasionál Austrália, ne'ebé Sue O'Connor lidera, mak ke'e iha ne'ebá. Ninia atun nia ruin, ho idade maizumenus tinan 42 000, no ninia anzól kulit-tasi halo nia famozu iha mundu. Fatin rua ne'e hatudu katak timoroan dahuluk sira hela besik tasi no hatene di'ak tasi nia riku-soin.
text.pt: Laili é um abrigo rochoso em Manatuto, no norte do país. As suas camadas mais antigas com vestígios humanos têm cerca de 44 000 anos e, por baixo, há camadas sem sinais de pessoas, o que ajuda a fixar a data de chegada. Os habitantes de Laili comiam marisco, peixe e animais de terra, como ratos. Jerimalai é um abrigo de calcário perto de Tutuala, no extremo leste. Foi escavado por equipas da Universidade Nacional Australiana dirigidas por Sue O'Connor. Os seus ossos de atum, com cerca de 42 000 anos, e os seus anzóis de concha tornaram-no famoso no mundo. Os dois sítios mostram que os primeiros timorenses viviam perto do mar e conheciam bem os seus recursos.
text.en: Laili is a rock shelter in Manatuto, in the north of the country. Its oldest layers with human traces are about 44,000 years old, and below them there are layers with no sign of people, which helps to pin down the date of arrival. The people of Laili ate shellfish, fish and land animals such as rats. Jerimalai is a limestone shelter near Tutuala, at the eastern tip of the country. It was excavated by teams from the Australian National University led by Sue O'Connor. Its tuna bones, about 42,000 years old, and its shell fish hooks made it famous around the world. The two sites show that the first Timorese lived near the sea and knew its resources well.
text.id: Laili adalah ceruk batu di Manatuto, di bagian utara negara ini. Lapisan tertuanya yang mengandung jejak manusia berumur sekitar 44.000 tahun, dan di bawahnya ada lapisan tanpa tanda-tanda manusia, yang membantu memastikan waktu kedatangan. Penghuni Laili memakan kerang, ikan, dan hewan darat seperti tikus. Jerimalai adalah ceruk batu kapur di dekat Tutuala, di ujung timur negara ini. Situs ini digali oleh tim-tim dari Universitas Nasional Australia yang dipimpin Sue O'Connor. Tulang tunanya yang berumur sekitar 42.000 tahun dan kailnya dari cangkang kerang membuat situs ini terkenal di dunia. Kedua situs ini menunjukkan bahwa orang Timor pertama tinggal di dekat laut dan sangat mengenal kekayaannya.

heading.tet: Lene Hara no Matja Kuru, iha Lautein
heading.pt: Lene Hara e Matja Kuru, em Lautém
heading.en: Lene Hara and Matja Kuru, in Lautém
heading.id: Lene Hara dan Matja Kuru, di Lautém

text.tet: Lene Hara mak fatuk-kuak boot ida iha área Tutuala, ho estalaktite no odamatan luan, iha Parke Nasionál Nino Konis Santana nia laran. Ke'e sira hetan kulit-tasi nia kanutu (kontas) no rastu seluk ho idade liu tinan 30 000, no ninia didin sira iha imajen tuan liu balu iha nasaun. Iha rai-laran liu, besik lagoa Ira Lalaro, iha fatuk-kuak Matja Kuru sira. Ema uza Matja Kuru 2 dala uluk maizumenus tinan 40 000 liubá, no fatin ne'e rai istória naruk tebes ida, to'o tinan rihun hirak ikus ne'e. Iha ninia kamada foun liu sira mosu sanan-rai, animál hakiak no asu tuan liu ida iha rejiaun, ho idade maizumenus tinan 3 000.
text.pt: Lene Hara é uma grande gruta da zona de Tutuala, com estalactites e uma entrada larga, dentro do Parque Nacional Nino Konis Santana. As escavações encontraram contas de concha e outros vestígios com mais de 30 000 anos, e as suas paredes têm algumas das imagens mais antigas do país. Mais para o interior, junto à lagoa Ira Lalaro, ficam as grutas de Matja Kuru. A Matja Kuru 2 foi usada pela primeira vez há cerca de 40 000 anos e guarda uma história muito longa, até aos últimos milhares de anos. Nas suas camadas mais recentes aparecem cerâmica, animais domésticos e um dos cães mais antigos da região, com cerca de 3000 anos.
text.en: Lene Hara is a large cave in the Tutuala area, with stalactites and a wide entrance, inside Nino Konis Santana National Park. Excavations found shell beads and other remains more than 30,000 years old, and its walls have some of the oldest images in the country. Further inland, by Lake Ira Lalaro, are the Matja Kuru caves. Matja Kuru 2 was first used about 40,000 years ago and holds a very long history, up to the last few thousand years. Its most recent layers contain pottery, domestic animals and one of the oldest dogs in the region, about 3,000 years old.
text.id: Lene Hara adalah gua besar di kawasan Tutuala, dengan stalaktit dan mulut gua yang lebar, di dalam Taman Nasional Nino Konis Santana. Penggalian menemukan manik-manik dari cangkang kerang dan sisa-sisa lain yang berumur lebih dari 30.000 tahun, dan dindingnya memuat sebagian gambar tertua di negara ini. Lebih ke pedalaman, di dekat Danau Ira Lalaro, terdapat gua-gua Matja Kuru. Matja Kuru 2 pertama kali dipakai sekitar 40.000 tahun lalu dan menyimpan sejarah yang sangat panjang, sampai beberapa ribu tahun terakhir. Di lapisan-lapisannya yang paling muda muncul tembikar, hewan peliharaan, dan salah satu anjing tertua di kawasan ini, yang berumur sekitar 3.000 tahun.

heading.tet: Fatuk-kuak sira iha Baukau no ke'e dahuluk sira
heading.pt: As grutas de Baucau e as primeiras escavações
heading.en: The caves of Baucau and the first excavations

text.tet: Iha tinan 1966 no 1967, arkeólogu Ian Glover halo ke'e sientífiku dahuluk iha fatuk-kuak sira Timór-Leste nian, iha fatin sira iha munisípiu Baukau ohin loron, hanesan Uai Bobo 1 no 2, besik Venilale, Lie Siri no Bui Ceri Uato. Nia hetan ekipamentu fatuk, hahán nia rastu, laho boot sira-nia ruin no, iha kamada foun liu sira, sanan-rai no animál sira-nia ruin ne'ebé ema lori mai. Ninia livru kona-ba ke'e sira-ne'e, ne'ebé sai iha tinan 1986, mak durante tempu naruk fonte prinsipál kona-ba Timór nia pre-istória. Depois, peskizadór seluk estuda fali ninia sasán sira ho métodu foun no hadi'a data sira.
text.pt: Em 1966 e 1967, o arqueólogo Ian Glover fez as primeiras escavações científicas em grutas de Timor-Leste, em locais do atual município de Baucau, como Uai Bobo 1 e 2, perto de Venilale, Lie Siri e Bui Ceri Uato. Encontrou ferramentas de pedra, restos de comida, ossos de ratos gigantes e, nas camadas mais recentes, cerâmica e ossos de animais trazidos pelas pessoas. O seu livro sobre estas escavações, publicado em 1986, foi durante muito tempo a principal fonte sobre a pré-história de Timor. Mais tarde, outros investigadores voltaram a estudar os seus materiais com novos métodos e afinaram as datas.
text.en: In 1966 and 1967 the archaeologist Ian Glover carried out the first scientific excavations in caves in Timor-Leste, at sites in today's Baucau municipality such as Uai Bobo 1 and 2 (near Venilale), Lie Siri and Bui Ceri Uato. He found stone tools, food remains, bones of giant rats and, in the most recent layers, pottery and bones of animals brought by people. His book about these excavations, published in 1986, was for a long time the main source on the prehistory of Timor. Later, other researchers studied his materials again with new methods and refined the dates.
text.id: Pada 1966 dan 1967, arkeolog Ian Glover melakukan penggalian ilmiah pertama di gua-gua Timor-Leste, di lokasi-lokasi yang kini termasuk munisipalitas Baucau, seperti Uai Bobo 1 dan 2 (dekat Venilale), Lie Siri, dan Bui Ceri Uato. Ia menemukan alat batu, sisa makanan, tulang tikus raksasa, dan, di lapisan yang paling muda, tembikar serta tulang hewan yang dibawa manusia. Bukunya tentang penggalian ini, yang terbit pada 1986, lama menjadi sumber utama tentang prasejarah Timor. Kemudian, peneliti lain mempelajari kembali bahan-bahannya dengan metode baru dan memperbaiki penanggalannya.

text.tet: Ba komunidade barak, fatuk-kuak sira la'ós fatin arkeolójiku de'it. Balu lulik, liga ho bei'ala sira, ho istória orijen nian no ho seremónia sira, liuliu ba Fataluku sira iha Lautein. Tan ne'e, arkeólogu sira husu lisensa ba lia-na'in no xefe lokál sira, no serbisu hamutuk ho komunidade no estudante timoroan sira. Vizitante sira tenke bá ho matadalan lokál ida, husu lisensa no la lori fatuk, ruin, kulit-tasi ka sanan-rai, tanba sasán ida ne'ebé sai husi ninia fatin lakon informasaun ne'ebé nia rai. La bele mós kaer didin sira ka hakerek iha sira-nia leten. Nune'e, fatuk-kuak sira kontinua konta timoroan dahuluk sira-nia istória ba jerasaun sira tuirmai.
text.pt: Para muitas comunidades, as grutas não são só sítios arqueológicos. Algumas são lulik, sagradas, ligadas aos antepassados, a histórias de origem e a cerimónias, sobretudo entre os fataluku de Lautém. Por isso, os arqueólogos pedem autorização aos lia-na'in e aos chefes locais e trabalham com as comunidades e com estudantes timorenses. Os visitantes devem ir com um guia local, pedir licença e não levar pedras, ossos, conchas ou cerâmica, porque cada objeto tirado do seu lugar perde a informação que guardava. Também não se deve tocar nas paredes nem escrever nelas. Assim, as grutas continuarão a contar a história dos primeiros timorenses às próximas gerações.
text.en: For many communities, caves are not just archaeological sites. Some are lulik, sacred, linked to the ancestors, to origin stories and to ceremonies, especially among the Fataluku of Lautém. That is why archaeologists ask permission from the lia-na'in and local chiefs and work with the communities and with Timorese students. Visitors should go with a local guide, ask permission and not take away stones, bones, shells or pottery, because every object taken from its place loses the information it held. Nor should anyone touch the walls or write on them. In this way, the caves will go on telling the story of the first Timorese to future generations.
text.id: Bagi banyak masyarakat, gua bukan sekadar situs arkeologi. Sebagian gua bersifat lulik, sakral, terkait dengan leluhur, kisah asal-usul, dan upacara, terutama di kalangan orang Fataluku di Lautém. Karena itu, arkeolog meminta izin kepada para lia-na'in dan pemimpin setempat serta bekerja bersama masyarakat dan pelajar Timor. Pengunjung sebaiknya datang bersama pemandu setempat, meminta izin, dan tidak membawa pulang batu, tulang, cangkang kerang, atau tembikar, karena setiap benda yang dipindahkan dari tempatnya kehilangan informasi yang disimpannya. Dinding gua juga tidak boleh disentuh atau ditulisi. Dengan begitu, gua-gua ini akan terus menceritakan kisah orang Timor pertama kepada generasi mendatang.

q.tet: Saida mak arkeólogu sira hetan iha fatuk-kuak ida nia kamada sira?

q.tet: Tanba saida mak karbonu-14 la bele sukat kamada ne'ebé iha idade tinan 100 000?

why.pt: O carbono-14 desaparece aos poucos; depois de cerca de 50 000 anos resta pouco para medir. Para camadas mais antigas usa-se a luminescência ou o urânio.
why.en: Carbon-14 disappears little by little; after about 50,000 years very little is left to measure. For older layers, luminescence or uranium is used.
why.id: Karbon-14 hilang sedikit demi sedikit; setelah sekitar 50.000 tahun, yang tersisa terlalu sedikit untuk diukur. Untuk lapisan yang lebih tua, dipakai luminesensi atau uranium.

title.tet: Arte iha fatuk-kuak: pintura no imajen ko'a iha fatuk
title.pt: Arte rupestre: imagens pintadas e gravadas nas grutas
title.en: Rock art: images painted and carved in the caves
title.id: Seni cadas: gambar yang dilukis dan dipahat di gua

summary.tet: Iha fatuk-kuak sira Lautein nian, liuliu iha área Tutuala, iha pintura mean no imajen ko'a iha fatuk ne'ebé ema halo durante tinan rihun barak. Iha liman nia marka, ema nia oin ne'ebé ko'a iha fatuk ho idade liu tinan 10 000, no pintura barak ho ró, ema no animál. Sira mak Timór-Leste nia patrimóniu folin-boot, no ba Fataluku sira fatin ne'ebé presiza respeitu.
summary.pt: Nas grutas e abrigos de Lautém, sobretudo à volta de Tutuala, há pinturas vermelhas e imagens gravadas na rocha feitas ao longo de milhares de anos. Há mãos em negativo, rostos humanos gravados com mais de 10 000 anos e muitos barcos, pessoas e animais. São um tesouro do património de Timor-Leste e, para os fataluku, lugares que pedem respeito.
summary.en: In the caves and rock shelters of Lautém, especially around Tutuala, there are red paintings and images carved into the rock, made over thousands of years. There are hand stencils, carved human faces more than 10,000 years old, and many boats, people and animals. They are a treasure of Timor-Leste's heritage and, for the Fataluku, places that call for respect.
summary.id: Di gua dan ceruk batu di Lautém, terutama di sekitar Tutuala, terdapat lukisan merah dan gambar yang dipahat di batu, yang dibuat selama ribuan tahun. Ada cap tangan, wajah manusia berpahat yang berumur lebih dari 10.000 tahun, serta banyak gambar perahu, manusia, dan hewan. Semua itu adalah harta warisan Timor-Leste dan, bagi orang Fataluku, tempat yang menuntut rasa hormat.

text.tet: Iha arte iha fatuk nia tipu boot rua. Ema halo pintura sira barak liu ho okre, rai ida ho besi barak ne'ebé ema fai no kahur ho bee. Sira tau kór ho liman-fuan, ho pinsél simples ka huu ho ibun. Atu halo liman nia marka, ema tau liman iha didin no huu tinta haleu nia, no liman nia forma hela iha fatuk. Petróglifu mak imajen ne'ebé ema ko'a ka baku iha fatuk rasik ho ekipamentu fatuk. Susar atu hatene arte nia idade, tanba tinta iha karbonu uitoan de'it. Tan ne'e, sientista sira sukat kamada minerál mihis sira ne'ebé mosu iha imajen nia leten ka okos, ho métodu urániu: ida-ne'e fó idade mínimu ka máximu.
text.pt: Há dois grandes tipos de arte rupestre. As pinturas eram feitas sobretudo com ocre, uma terra rica em ferro que se mói e se mistura com água, aplicada com os dedos, com pincéis simples ou soprada. Para fazer uma mão em negativo, encostava-se a mão à parede e soprava-se tinta à volta, e ficava o contorno da mão. Os petróglifos são imagens gravadas ou picotadas na própria rocha com ferramentas de pedra. Datar a arte é difícil, porque a tinta tem pouco carbono. Por isso, os cientistas datam as finas crostas minerais que se formam por cima ou por baixo das imagens, com o método do urânio, que dá uma idade mínima ou máxima.
text.en: There are two main kinds of rock art. Paintings were made mostly with ochre, an iron-rich earth that is ground and mixed with water, then applied with the fingers, with simple brushes or by blowing. To make a hand stencil, a person pressed a hand against the wall and blew paint around it, leaving the outline of the hand. Petroglyphs are images carved or pecked into the rock itself with stone tools. Dating the art is difficult, because the paint contains little carbon. So scientists date the thin mineral crusts that form over or under the images, using the uranium method, which gives a minimum or maximum age.
text.id: Ada dua jenis utama seni cadas. Lukisan terutama dibuat dengan oker, tanah kaya besi yang digiling dan dicampur air, lalu dioleskan dengan jari, dengan kuas sederhana, atau disemburkan. Untuk membuat cap tangan, orang menempelkan tangan ke dinding dan menyemburkan cat di sekelilingnya, sehingga tertinggal garis bentuk tangan. Petroglif adalah gambar yang dipahat atau dipukul-pukul langsung pada batu dengan alat batu. Menentukan umur seni ini sulit, karena catnya hanya sedikit mengandung karbon. Karena itu, ilmuwan menentukan umur kerak mineral tipis yang terbentuk di atas atau di bawah gambar, dengan metode uranium, yang memberikan umur minimum atau maksimum.

text.tet: Iha fatuk-kuak Lene Hara, besik Tutuala, arkeólogu sira hetan ema nia oin simples sira ne'ebé ema ko'a iha fatuk. Iha tinan 2010, Sue O'Connor nia ekipa publika iha revista Antiquity petróglifu ida nia idade. Kamada minerál ida ne'ebé liga ho imajen ne'e hatudu katak ema ko'a nia iha tempu jelu nia rohan, liu tinan 10 000 liubá (maizumenus tinan 10 000 to'o 12 000). Imajen sira-ne'e iha oin ema nian tuan liu balu ne'ebé ema hatene iha rejiaun ne'e. Revista National Geographic Indonézia mós konta kona-ba deskobrimentu ne'e. Se mak ko'a sira no tanba saida, ita seidauk hatene.
text.pt: Na gruta de Lene Hara, perto de Tutuala, os arqueólogos encontraram rostos humanos simples gravados na rocha. Em 2010, a equipa de Sue O'Connor publicou na revista Antiquity a datação de um destes petróglifos. Uma crosta mineral ligada à gravura indica que ela foi feita no fim da Idade do Gelo, há mais de 10 000 anos (cerca de 10 000 a 12 000 anos). Estão entre as imagens de rostos humanos mais antigas conhecidas na região. A revista National Geographic Indonésia também contou esta descoberta. Quem os gravou, e porquê, continua a ser um mistério.
text.en: In Lene Hara cave, near Tutuala, archaeologists found simple human faces carved into the rock. In 2010 Sue O'Connor's team published the date of one of these petroglyphs in the journal Antiquity. A mineral crust linked to the carving shows that it was made at the end of the Ice Age, more than 10,000 years ago (about 10,000 to 12,000 years). They are among the oldest known images of human faces in the region. The magazine National Geographic Indonesia also told the story of this discovery. Who carved them, and why, remains a mystery.
text.id: Di Gua Lene Hara, dekat Tutuala, arkeolog menemukan wajah manusia sederhana yang dipahat di batu. Pada 2010, tim Sue O'Connor menerbitkan penanggalan salah satu petroglif ini di jurnal Antiquity. Kerak mineral yang terkait dengan pahatan itu menunjukkan bahwa pahatan dibuat pada akhir Zaman Es, lebih dari 10.000 tahun lalu (sekitar 10.000 sampai 12.000 tahun). Gambar-gambar ini termasuk gambar wajah manusia tertua yang diketahui di kawasan ini. Majalah National Geographic Indonesia juga memberitakan penemuan ini. Siapa yang memahatnya, dan mengapa, masih menjadi misteri.

heading.tet: Liman sira husi tinan rihun barak liubá
heading.pt: Mãos de há milhares de anos
heading.en: Hands from thousands of years ago

text.tet: Iha tinan 2020, peskizadór sira Standish, García-Diez, O'Connor no Oliveira deskreve liman nia marka 16 ka liu iha fatuk-kuak Lene Hara. Sira hanoin katak marka sira-ne'e parte husi tradisaun ida ne'ebé tuan liu duké pintura barak iha Timór, karik husi tempu jelu. Ida-ne'e tuir deskobrimentu seluk: iha fatuk-kuak nia kamada minerál sira-nia okos iha kór mean nia kamada ida ho idade tinan 24 000 to'o 29 000, maski pintura sira ne'ebé ita haree ohin iha idade menus husi maizumenus tinan 6 300. Liman nia marka iha fatuk-kuak sira iha mundu tomak, no iha Timór sira liga ema dahuluk sira ho povu sira iha illa seluk iha rejiaun.
text.pt: Em 2020, os investigadores Standish, García-Diez, O'Connor e Oliveira descreveram pelo menos 16 mãos em negativo na gruta de Lene Hara. Pensam que pertencem a uma tradição mais antiga do que a maior parte das pinturas de Timor, provavelmente da Idade do Gelo. Isto combina com outra descoberta: por baixo das crostas minerais da gruta há uma camada de pigmento vermelho com 24 000 a 29 000 anos, embora as pinturas que hoje se veem tenham menos de cerca de 6300 anos. Há mãos em negativo em grutas de todo o mundo, e em Timor elas ligam os primeiros habitantes aos povos de outras ilhas da região.
text.en: In 2020 the researchers Standish, García-Diez, O'Connor and Oliveira described at least 16 hand stencils in Lene Hara cave. They think that the stencils belong to a tradition older than most of Timor's paintings, probably from the Ice Age. This fits with another discovery: beneath the cave's mineral crusts there is a layer of red pigment 24,000 to 29,000 years old, although the paintings that can be seen today are less than about 6,300 years old. Hand stencils are found in caves all over the world, and on Timor they link the first inhabitants with the peoples of other islands in the region.
text.id: Pada 2020, peneliti Standish, García-Diez, O'Connor, dan Oliveira mendeskripsikan sedikitnya 16 cap tangan di Gua Lene Hara. Mereka menduga cap tangan ini termasuk tradisi yang lebih tua daripada sebagian besar lukisan di Timor, kemungkinan dari Zaman Es. Hal ini sesuai dengan penemuan lain: di bawah kerak mineral gua terdapat lapisan pigmen merah berumur 24.000 sampai 29.000 tahun, meskipun lukisan yang terlihat sekarang berumur kurang dari sekitar 6.300 tahun. Cap tangan ditemukan di gua-gua di seluruh dunia, dan di Timor cap tangan menghubungkan para penghuni pertama dengan bangsa-bangsa di pulau lain di kawasan ini.

text.tet: Pintura barak liu ne'ebé ita haree ohin, ema halo iha tinan rihun hirak ikus ne'e, ho kór mean, iha estilu ida ne'ebé espesialista sira bolu Tradisaun Pintura Austronézia. Iha estudu ida husi tinan 2003, Sue O'Connor deskreve fatin pintura barak iha Timór-Leste nia rohan loro-sa'e. Aleinde ema nia figura ki'ik sira, imajen ne'ebé mosu barak liu mak ró, dala barak ho ulun aas no kleuk, no ho remu atu ukun ró nia dalan. Iha mós animál no sinál seluk. Imajen balu hanesan hatudu baliun metál ho fatin atu tama ai-kain, no ida-ne'e liga arte ne'e ho metál nia tempu. Fatuk-kuak Ili Kére Kére, besik Tutuala, mak fatin ida ne'ebé riku liu ho pintura sira-ne'e.
text.pt: A maior parte das pinturas que hoje se veem foi feita nos últimos milhares de anos, a vermelho, num estilo que os especialistas chamam Tradição de Pintura Austronésia. Num estudo de 2003, Sue O'Connor descreveu vários sítios pintados no extremo leste de Timor-Leste. Além de pequenas figuras humanas, o tema mais comum são os barcos, muitas vezes com proas altas e inclinadas e com remos de governo. Há também animais e outros sinais. Algumas imagens parecem mostrar machados de metal com encaixe para o cabo, o que liga esta arte à Idade do Metal. O abrigo de Ili Kére Kére, perto de Tutuala, é um dos sítios mais ricos destas pinturas.
text.en: Most of the paintings that can be seen today were made in the last few thousand years, in red, in a style that specialists call the Austronesian Painting Tradition. In a 2003 study, Sue O'Connor described several painted sites at the eastern tip of Timor-Leste. Apart from small human figures, the most common subject is boats, often with high, raked prows and with steering oars. There are also animals and other signs. Some images seem to show metal axes with a socket for the handle, which links this art to the Metal Age. The Ili Kére Kére shelter, near Tutuala, is one of the richest sites for these paintings.
text.id: Sebagian besar lukisan yang terlihat sekarang dibuat dalam beberapa ribu tahun terakhir, dengan warna merah, dalam gaya yang oleh para ahli disebut Tradisi Lukisan Austronesia. Dalam penelitian tahun 2003, Sue O'Connor mendeskripsikan beberapa situs lukisan di ujung timur Timor-Leste. Selain sosok manusia kecil, tema yang paling umum adalah perahu, sering dengan haluan tinggi yang miring dan dengan dayung kemudi. Ada juga hewan dan tanda-tanda lain. Beberapa gambar tampaknya memperlihatkan kapak logam dengan lubang untuk tangkainya (kapak corong), yang menghubungkan seni ini dengan Zaman Logam. Ceruk Ili Kére Kére, dekat Tutuala, adalah salah satu situs yang paling kaya akan lukisan seperti ini.

text.tet: Pintura sira moris tinan rihun barak, maibé sira bele aat iha minutu balu de'it. Liman nia kosar no mina, ahi-suar husi ahi ne'ebé ema sunu, hakerek iha didin no rai-rahun ne'ebé vizitante sira hasa'e halakon tinta no hakotu kamada minerál ne'ebé rai data sira. Fatin barak iha Parke Nasionál Nino Konis Santana no lulik ba Fataluku sira. Tan ne'e, vizita tenke halo ho matadalan lokál, ho komunidade nia lisensa no la kaer didin sira. Foti foto la ho flash no hakerek imajen sira-nia fatin ajuda sientista no eskola sira atu estuda sira la ho estraga. Arte iha fatuk mak bei'ala sira-nia mensajen ne'ebé ita sei bele lee.
text.pt: As pinturas sobreviveram milhares de anos, mas podem estragar-se em minutos. O suor e a gordura das mãos, o fumo das fogueiras, os grafitos e o pó levantado pelos visitantes apagam a tinta e partem as crostas que guardam as datas. Muitos destes lugares ficam no Parque Nacional Nino Konis Santana e são lulik para os fataluku. Por isso, as visitas devem ser feitas com guias locais, com licença da comunidade e sem tocar nas paredes. Fotografar sem flash e registar onde estão as imagens ajuda cientistas e escolas a estudá-las sem as estragar. A arte rupestre é uma mensagem dos antepassados que ainda podemos ler.
text.en: The paintings have survived for thousands of years, but they can be damaged in minutes. Sweat and grease from hands, smoke from fires, graffiti and the dust raised by visitors wipe away the paint and break the crusts that hold the dates. Many of these places are in Nino Konis Santana National Park and are lulik for the Fataluku. So visits should be made with local guides, with the community's permission and without touching the walls. Taking photographs without flash and recording where the images are helps scientists and schools to study them without damaging them. Rock art is a message from the ancestors that we can still read.
text.id: Lukisan-lukisan ini bertahan ribuan tahun, tetapi bisa rusak dalam hitungan menit. Keringat dan minyak dari tangan, asap api unggun, coretan, dan debu yang diterbangkan pengunjung menghapus cat dan memecahkan kerak yang menyimpan penanggalan. Banyak tempat ini berada di Taman Nasional Nino Konis Santana dan bersifat lulik bagi orang Fataluku. Karena itu, kunjungan harus dilakukan bersama pemandu setempat, dengan izin masyarakat, dan tanpa menyentuh dinding. summary.tet: Maizumenus tinan 3 500 liubá, moris iha Timór hahú muda: sanan-rai mosu, no ai-horis ba to'os no animál hanesan asu no fahi to'o ho ró. Buat foun sira-ne'e to'o hamutuk ho ró-na'in sira ne'ebé ko'alia lian Austronézia, no namkari neineik. Ema kontinua kaer ikan no buka hahán iha natureza, maibé knua no to'os sira muda illa ne'e.
summary.pt: Há cerca de 3500 anos, a vida em Timor começou a mudar: apareceu a cerâmica e chegaram de barco plantas cultivadas e animais como o cão e o porco. Estas novidades vieram com navegadores de línguas austronésias e espalharam-se aos poucos. A pesca e a recolha continuaram, mas as aldeias e os campos foram transformando a ilha.
summary.en: About 3,500 years ago, life on Timor began to change: pottery appeared, and cultivated plants and animals such as the dog and the pig arrived by boat. These new things came with seafarers who spoke Austronesian languages, and they spread little by little. Fishing and gathering continued, but villages and fields gradually transformed the island.
summary.id: Sekitar 3.500 tahun lalu, kehidupan di Timor mulai berubah: tembikar muncul, dan tanaman budi daya serta hewan seperti anjing dan babi datang dengan perahu. Hal-hal baru ini dibawa oleh para pelaut penutur bahasa Austronesia dan menyebar sedikit demi sedikit. Menangkap ikan dan meramu terus berlanjut, tetapi kampung dan ladang lambat laun mengubah pulau ini.

heading.pt: O Neolítico: uma nova forma de viver
heading.en: The Neolithic: a new way of life

text.tet: Arkeólogu sira bolu Neolítiku ba tempu ne'ebé ema hahú kuda ai-horis, hakiak animál no halo sanan-rai. Iha Ázia Sudeste nia illa sira, mudansa sira-ne'e liga liuliu ho povu sira ne'ebé ko'alia lian Austronézia. Sira hahú namkari husi Taiwan maizumenus tinan 4 000 to'o 5 000 liubá, no la'o ho ró husi illa ida ba illa seluk. Iha Timór-Leste, tuir ke'e sira, Neolítiku nia sinál sira hahú maizumenus tinan 3 500 liubá. Mudansa ne'e la akontese derepente: durante tempu naruk, ema kontinua kaer ikan, foti kulit-tasi no kasa, no neineik sira kahur téknika foun sira ho buat ne'ebé sira hatene ona. Povu sira ne'ebé hela ona iha Timór mós simu buat foun sira.
text.pt: Os arqueólogos chamam Neolítico à época em que as pessoas começaram a cultivar plantas, criar animais e fazer cerâmica. No Sudeste Asiático insular, estas mudanças estão ligadas sobretudo aos povos de línguas austronésias, que começaram a espalhar-se a partir de Taiwan há uns 4000 a 5000 anos, navegando de ilha em ilha. Em Timor-Leste, segundo as escavações, os sinais do Neolítico começam há cerca de 3500 anos. A mudança não foi súbita: durante muito tempo, as pessoas continuaram a pescar, a apanhar marisco e a caçar, e juntaram aos poucos as novas técnicas ao que já sabiam. Os povos que já viviam em Timor também adotaram as novidades.
text.en: Archaeologists use the name Neolithic for the period when people began to grow plants, raise animals and make pottery. In Island Southeast Asia, these changes are linked mainly to the Austronesian-speaking peoples, who began to spread out from Taiwan some 4,000 to 5,000 years ago, sailing from island to island. In Timor-Leste, according to excavations, signs of the Neolithic begin about 3,500 years ago. The change was not sudden: for a long time people went on fishing, gathering shellfish and hunting, and little by little they added the new techniques to what they already knew. The peoples already living on Timor also took up the new ways.
text.id: Arkeolog menyebut Neolitikum untuk masa ketika manusia mulai menanam tumbuhan, memelihara hewan, dan membuat tembikar. Di Asia Tenggara kepulauan, perubahan ini terutama terkait dengan bangsa-bangsa penutur bahasa Austronesia, yang mulai menyebar dari Taiwan sekitar 4.000 sampai 5.000 tahun lalu, berlayar dari pulau ke pulau. Di Timor-Leste, menurut hasil penggalian, tanda-tanda Neolitikum dimulai sekitar 3.500 tahun lalu. Perubahan ini tidak terjadi tiba-tiba: lama sekali orang tetap menangkap ikan, mengumpulkan kerang, dan berburu, lalu sedikit demi sedikit menambahkan teknik-teknik baru pada apa yang sudah mereka ketahui. Bangsa-bangsa yang sudah tinggal di Timor juga ikut menerima hal-hal baru itu.

text.tet: Sanan-rai mak prova klaru liu ida husi Neolítiku. Sanan-rai nia pedasuk tuan liu iha fatuk-kuak sira Timór-Leste nian iha idade tinan 3 500 ka liu. Ema uza sanan atu te'in, nono no rai bee no hahán, no ida-ne'e muda sira-nia hahán: sira bele te'in modo-tahan, ai-han husi abut no kulit-tasi nia na'an to'o tasak. Arkeólogu sira estuda pedasuk ida-idak nia forma, dekorasaun no rai-tahu atu hatene nia mai husi ne'ebé no se ema halo iha fatin ne'e. Iha fatin foun liu, husi metál nia tempu, mós iha sanan-rai, no peskizadór sira rekoñese katak ita seidauk hatene barak kona-ba bainhira no oinsá sanan-rai to'o rejiaun ne'e. Ohin loron, knua balu iha Timór-Leste sei halo sanan ho liman.
text.pt: A cerâmica é uma das provas mais claras do Neolítico. Os fragmentos de potes de barro mais antigos das grutas de Timor-Leste têm pelo menos 3500 anos. Os potes serviam para cozinhar, ferver e guardar água e alimentos, e isso mudou a alimentação: passou a ser possível cozer bem legumes, raízes e marisco. Os arqueólogos estudam a forma, a decoração e o barro de cada fragmento para saber de onde veio e se foi feito no lugar. Em sítios mais recentes, da Idade do Metal, também há cerâmica, e os investigadores reconhecem que ainda se sabe pouco sobre quando e como a cerâmica chegou à região. Hoje ainda há aldeias timorenses que fazem potes à mão.
text.en: Pottery is one of the clearest signs of the Neolithic. The oldest fragments of clay pots from the caves of Timor-Leste are at least 3,500 years old. Pots were used to cook, boil and store water and food, and this changed people's diet: it became possible to cook vegetables, roots and shellfish thoroughly. Archaeologists study the shape, decoration and clay of each fragment to find out where it came from and whether it was made locally. There is also pottery at more recent sites from the Metal Age, and researchers admit that little is yet known about when and how pottery reached the region. Today some Timorese villages still make pots by hand.
text.id: Tembikar adalah salah satu bukti paling jelas dari Neolitikum. Pecahan periuk tanah liat tertua dari gua-gua Timor-Leste berumur sedikitnya 3.500 tahun. Periuk dipakai untuk memasak, merebus, serta menyimpan air dan makanan, dan hal ini mengubah pola makan: sayuran, umbi, dan kerang kini bisa dimasak sampai matang. Arkeolog mempelajari bentuk, hiasan, dan tanah liat setiap pecahan untuk mengetahui asalnya dan apakah pecahan itu dibuat di tempat. Di situs-situs yang lebih muda, dari Zaman Logam, juga ada tembikar, dan para peneliti mengakui bahwa masih sedikit yang diketahui tentang kapan dan bagaimana tembikar sampai ke kawasan ini. Sampai sekarang masih ada kampung di Timor-Leste yang membuat periuk dengan tangan.

heading.tet: Animál sira ne'ebé mai ho ró

text.tet: Timór la iha mamíferu boot orijinál, aleinde Stegodon ne'ebé lakon ona; kuaze animál boot hotu ne'ebé ita haree ohin, ema mak lori mai. Asu tuan liu ne'ebé ema hatene iha Timór-Leste, sira hetan iha fatuk-kuak Matja Kuru 2, no nia idade maizumenus tinan 3 000. Ida-ne'e asu nia rejistu tuan liu ida iha rejiaun haleu Austrália no Nova Giné. Fahi mós to'o ho ró, no ema mak lori lekirauk mai iha tinan rihun hirak ikus ne'e. Ema mós lori bibi, bibi-rusa no kuskus iha tempu oioin. Data loloos ba animál ida-idak sei iha estudu: estudu ida husi tinan 2023 kona-ba animál sira iha fatuk-kuak Timór-Leste nian halibur data ne'ebé ema hatene.
text.pt: Timor não tinha grandes mamíferos nativos, além do Stegodon já desaparecido; quase todos os que hoje vemos foram trazidos pelas pessoas. O cão mais antigo conhecido em Timor-Leste foi encontrado na gruta Matja Kuru 2 e tem cerca de 3000 anos, um dos registos de cães mais antigos da região à volta da Austrália e da Nova Guiné. Os porcos também chegaram de barco, e os macacos-de-cauda-longa (lekirauk) foram trazidos pelas pessoas nos últimos milhares de anos. As cabras, o veado-de-timor e o cuscus vieram também com as pessoas, em épocas diferentes. As datas exatas de cada chegada continuam em estudo: um trabalho de 2023 sobre os animais das grutas de Timor-Leste reúne as datas conhecidas.
text.en: Timor had no large native mammals, apart from the long-vanished Stegodon; almost all of those we see today were brought by people. The oldest known dog in Timor-Leste was found in Matja Kuru 2 cave and is about 3,000 years old, one of the oldest dog records in the region around Australia and New Guinea. Pigs also came by boat, and long-tailed macaques (lekirauk) were brought by people in the last few thousand years. Goats, the Timor deer and the cuscus also came with people, at different times. The exact dates of each arrival are still being studied: a 2023 study of the animals from the caves of Timor-Leste brings together the known dates.
text.id: Timor tidak memiliki mamalia asli yang besar, selain Stegodon yang sudah lama punah; hampir semua yang kita lihat sekarang dibawa oleh manusia. Anjing tertua yang diketahui di Timor-Leste ditemukan di Gua Matja Kuru 2 dan berumur sekitar 3.000 tahun, salah satu catatan anjing tertua di kawasan sekitar Australia dan Nugini. Babi juga datang dengan perahu, dan monyet ekor panjang (lekirauk) dibawa manusia dalam beberapa ribu tahun terakhir. Kambing, rusa timor, dan kuskus juga datang bersama manusia, pada masa yang berbeda-beda. Tanggal pasti kedatangan masing-masing hewan masih diteliti: sebuah penelitian tahun 2023 tentang hewan-hewan dari gua di Timor-Leste menghimpun tanggal-tanggal yang sudah diketahui.

heading.pt: Campos, florestas e mudanças na ilha
heading.en: Fields, forests and changes on the island
heading.id: Ladang, hutan, dan perubahan di pulau

text.tet: Ema hanoin katak agrikultór dahuluk sira iha Timór kuda liuliu ai-horis ho abut no ai-fuan ne'ebé ema bele han, hanesan talas no hudi; batar to'o de'it depois tinan 1500, husi Amérika. Karik sira ko'a ai-laran, sunu ai-horis no kuda, no muda ba to'os foun bainhira rai kole ona, hanesan ema sei halo iha área balu. Durante tinan rihun barak, serbisu ne'e muda paizajen, no ai-laran orijinál sira menus barak. Sientista sira hanoin katak ai-laran lakon ne'e mak kauza prinsipál ba laho boot no laho seluk ne'ebé iha de'it iha Timór atu lakon. Iha tinan 1522, Pigafetta hakerek katak iha illa ne'e iha hare, hudi, tohu, karau, fahi no bibi.
text.pt: Pensa-se que os primeiros agricultores de Timor cultivavam sobretudo plantas de raiz e de fruto, como o inhame, o taro e a banana; o milho só chegou depois de 1500, vindo das Américas. Provavelmente abriam clareiras na floresta, queimavam a vegetação e plantavam, mudando de campo quando a terra se cansava, como ainda se faz em algumas zonas. Ao longo de milhares de anos, este trabalho transformou a paisagem, e as florestas originais diminuíram muito. Os cientistas pensam que esta perda de floresta foi a principal causa do desaparecimento dos ratos gigantes e de outros ratos que só existiam em Timor. Em 1522, Pigafetta registou na ilha arroz, bananas, cana-de-açúcar, búfalos, porcos e cabras.
text.en: It is thought that Timor's first farmers grew mainly root and fruit crops, such as yams, taro and bananas; maize arrived only after 1500, from the Americas. They probably cleared patches of forest, burned the vegetation and planted, moving to a new field when the soil was worn out, as is still done in some areas. Over thousands of years this work transformed the landscape, and the original forests shrank greatly. Scientists think that this loss of forest was the main cause of the disappearance of the giant rats and other rats found only on Timor. In 1522 Pigafetta recorded rice, bananas, sugar cane, buffaloes, pigs and goats on the island.
text.id: Diduga petani pertama di Timor terutama menanam tanaman umbi dan buah, seperti ubi, talas, dan pisang; jagung baru datang setelah tahun 1500, dari benua Amerika. Mereka kemungkinan membuka hutan, membakar tumbuhannya, lalu menanam, dan berpindah ladang ketika tanahnya tidak subur lagi, seperti yang masih dilakukan di beberapa daerah. Selama ribuan tahun, pekerjaan ini mengubah bentang alam, dan hutan asli sangat berkurang. Ilmuwan menduga hilangnya hutan ini menjadi penyebab utama punahnya tikus raksasa dan tikus-tikus lain yang hanya ada di Timor. Pada 1522, Pigafetta mencatat adanya padi, pisang, tebu, kerbau, babi, dan kambing di pulau ini.

text.tet: Ai-horis foun, animál no sanan-rai to'o hamutuk ho ró-na'in sira ne'ebé ko'alia lian Austronézia, entre maizumenus tinan 4 500 no 3 000 liubá; estimativa sira la hanesan. Sira la to'o iha illa mamuk ida: sira hasoru povu sira ne'ebé hela ona iha Timór durante tinan rihun barak. Grupu rua ne'e troka sasán, hanoin no liafuan, no kaben malu. Tan ne'e, timoroan ohin loron mai husi grupu rua ne'e, no iha nasaun ne'e ema ko'alia lian Austronézia, hanesan Tetun no Mambai, no lian Papua, hanesan Fataluku no Makasae. Depois Neolítiku, metál nia tempu mai, ho sasán bronze no negósiu foun ho rai sira ne'ebé dook.
text.pt: As novas plantas, os animais e a cerâmica chegaram com navegadores que falavam línguas austronésias, entre há cerca de 4500 e 3000 anos; as estimativas variam. Não chegaram a uma ilha vazia: encontraram povos que viviam em Timor há dezenas de milhares de anos. Os dois grupos trocaram objetos, ideias e palavras, e casaram entre si. Por isso, os timorenses de hoje descendem de ambos, e no país falam-se línguas austronésias, como o tétum e o mambai, e línguas papuas, como o fataluku e o makasae. Depois do Neolítico veio a Idade do Metal, com objetos de bronze e novas trocas com terras distantes.
text.en: The new plants, the animals and pottery came with seafarers who spoke Austronesian languages, between about 4,500 and 3,000 years ago; estimates vary. They did not arrive on an empty island: they met peoples who had lived on Timor for tens of thousands of years. The two groups exchanged objects, ideas and words, and married each other. That is why today's Timorese descend from both, and the country's languages include Austronesian ones, such as Tetun and Mambai, and Papuan ones, such as Fataluku and Makasae. After the Neolithic came the Metal Age, with bronze objects and new exchanges with distant lands.
text.id: Tanaman baru, hewan, dan tembikar datang bersama para pelaut penutur bahasa Austronesia, antara sekitar 4.500 dan 3.000 tahun lalu; perkiraannya berbeda-beda. Mereka tidak tiba di pulau yang kosong: mereka bertemu bangsa-bangsa yang sudah tinggal di Timor selama puluhan ribu tahun. Kedua kelompok saling bertukar barang, gagasan, dan kata, serta saling menikah. Karena itu, orang Timor masa kini adalah keturunan keduanya, dan di negara ini dituturkan bahasa-bahasa Austronesia, seperti Tetun dan Mambai, serta bahasa-bahasa Papua, seperti Fataluku dan Makasae. Setelah Neolitikum datanglah Zaman Logam, dengan benda-benda perunggu dan pertukaran baru dengan negeri-negeri yang jauh.

review.notes: Neolithic in Timor-Leste from about 3,500 years ago (ANU publication record) and pottery at least 3,500 years old (IRD record, Galipaud et al.). Out of Taiwan about 4,000–5,000 years ago and Austronesian arrival 4,500–3,000 years ago follow tl.history.austronesian_papuan. Dog: Matja Kuru 2, 2886–3068 cal BP, one of the earliest in the wider region (JCU paper). Pigs, macaques ('in the last few thousand years'), goats, deer and cuscus as human introductions follow tl.nature.animals and Louys et al. 2023 — their exact dates were not checked (one popular source says cuscus about 3,000 years; not used). Early crops (yams, taro, bananas) and shifting cultivation are hypotheses, written as 'it is thought / probably' — check with recent archaeobotany. Maize after 1500 from the Americas: general knowledge. Pigafetta's 1522 list (rice, bananas, sugar cane, buffaloes, pigs, goats) from memory of his account — check. 'Some villages still make pots by hand' — see tl.culture.crafts. 'Little is known about when pottery arrived' reflects a 2020 Journal of Indo-Pacific Archaeology paper on Early Metal Age pottery (search summary). Period: -2500 (Austronesian arrival) to about 1 CE (start of the Metal Age, approximate). Timeline -2500 and -1500 reuse the titles of tl.history.austronesian_papuan on purpose. Tetun terms to check: Neolítiku, modo-tahan, nono (boil), ai-han husi abut, talas, hudi, tohu, batar, bibi-rusa, kuskus, kole (tired soil), téknika. EN/ID (2026-11-11): English and Indonesian translated by hand from the Portuguese and checked against the Tetun; Tetun and Portuguese not changed. Timeline titles shared between articles are translated identically. Terms (en/id): Neolithic/Neolitikum, Island Southeast Asia/Asia Tenggara kepulauan, clay pots/periuk tanah liat, yam/ubi, taro/talas, long-tailed macaque/monyet ekor panjang, Timor deer/rusa timor, cuscus/kuskus, Metal Age/Zaman Logam. The Tetun of 'Viziñu foun, lian foun' says 'tinan rihun barak' (many thousands of years) where the Portuguese says 'dezenas de milhares' (tens of thousands): the translations follow the Portuguese.

summary.tet: Uluk liu ema Europa sira, Timór parte ona husi negósiu nia rede ne'ebé liga illa sira ho Ázia kontinente. Tambór bronze tipu Dong Son, ho idade tinan 2 000 ka liu, to'o iha Baukau. Livru Xina husi sékulu 13, poema ida husi Java husi tinan 1365 no Antonio Pigafetta nia relatóriu husi tinan 1522 mak testu dahuluk balu ne'ebé ko'alia kona-ba illa ne'e.
summary.pt: Muito antes dos europeus, Timor já fazia parte de redes de comércio que ligavam as ilhas à Ásia continental. Tambores de bronze do tipo Dong Son, com pelo menos 2000 anos, chegaram até Baucau. Livros chineses do século XIII, um poema de Java de 1365 e o relato de Antonio Pigafetta de 1522 estão entre os primeiros textos que falam da ilha.
summary.en: Long before the Europeans, Timor was already part of trade networks that linked the islands with mainland Asia. Dong Son-type bronze drums, at least 2,000 years old, reached as far as Baucau. Chinese books from the 13th century, a poem from Java of 1365 and Antonio Pigafetta's account of 1522 are among the first texts that speak of the island.
summary.id: Jauh sebelum orang Eropa datang, Timor sudah menjadi bagian dari jaringan perdagangan yang menghubungkan pulau-pulau dengan daratan Asia. Nekara perunggu tipe Dong Son yang berumur sedikitnya 2.000 tahun sampai ke Baucau. Buku-buku Tiongkok dari abad ke-13, sebuah syair dari Jawa tahun 1365, dan catatan Antonio Pigafetta tahun 1522 termasuk teks-teks pertama yang membicarakan pulau ini.

heading.pt: A Idade do Metal chega a Timor

text.tet: Maizumenus tinan 2 000 liubá ka uluk liu, sasán metál hahú namkari iha Ázia Sudeste nia illa sira: baliun, pulseira no tambór bronze nian, no depois besi. Timór tama mós iha rede sira-ne'e. Arkeólogu sira Nuno Vasco Oliveira, Sue O'Connor no Peter Bellwood estuda tambór bronze no sasán kobre seluk ne'ebé ema hetan iha Timór-Leste. Sira haree katak arte iha fatuk-kuak Timór nian hatudu baliun ho fatin atu tama ai-kain, no katak iha kobre nia fonte ida iha Timór loro-monu. Tan ne'e sira hanoin katak karik ema iha Illa Sunda Ki'ik sira serbisu ona kobre no bronze iha pre-istória. Hodi troka metál, Timór bele fó sasán husi ai-laran no tasi.
text.pt: Há uns 2000 anos ou mais, objetos de metal começaram a circular pelas ilhas do Sudeste Asiático: machados, pulseiras e tambores de bronze, e mais tarde ferro. Timor entrou nestas redes. Os arqueólogos Nuno Vasco Oliveira, Sue O'Connor e Peter Bellwood estudaram tambores de bronze e outros objetos de cobre encontrados em Timor-Leste. Notaram que a arte rupestre timorense mostra machados com encaixe para o cabo e que existe uma fonte de cobre em Timor Ocidental; por isso, pensam que as Pequenas Ilhas de Sunda talvez tenham trabalhado o cobre e o bronze na pré-história. Em troca do metal, Timor podia oferecer produtos da floresta e do mar.
text.en: Some 2,000 years ago or earlier, metal objects began to circulate among the islands of Southeast Asia: bronze axes, bracelets and drums, and later iron. Timor joined these networks. The archaeologists Nuno Vasco Oliveira, Sue O'Connor and Peter Bellwood studied bronze drums and other copper objects found in Timor-Leste. They noted that Timorese rock art shows axes with a socket for the handle and that there is a source of copper in West Timor; so they think that people in the Lesser Sunda Islands may have worked copper and bronze in prehistoric times. In exchange for metal, Timor could offer products of the forest and the sea.
text.id: Sekitar 2.000 tahun lalu atau lebih awal, benda-benda logam mulai beredar di pulau-pulau Asia Tenggara: kapak, gelang, dan nekara perunggu, lalu kemudian besi. Timor ikut masuk ke dalam jaringan ini. Arkeolog Nuno Vasco Oliveira, Sue O'Connor, dan Peter Bellwood meneliti nekara perunggu dan benda-benda tembaga lain yang ditemukan di Timor-Leste. Mereka mencatat bahwa seni cadas Timor memperlihatkan kapak dengan lubang untuk tangkainya (kapak corong) dan bahwa ada sumber tembaga di Timor Barat; karena itu, mereka menduga orang di Kepulauan Sunda Kecil mungkin sudah mengolah tembaga dan perunggu pada masa prasejarah. Sebagai ganti logam, Timor bisa menawarkan hasil hutan dan laut.

heading.pt: Os tambores de bronze de Dong Son

text.tet: Tambór Dong Son nian mak tambór bronze boot sira ne'ebé ema halo iha fatin serbisu sira iha Vietname nia norte no Xina nia sul; sira-nia naran mai husi knua ida iha Vietname, fatin ne'ebé ema hatene kultura ne'e dala uluk. Tambór nia oin leten dala barak iha fitun ida iha klaran, no ninia sorin sira hatudu manu, ró no ema ho manu-fulun. Iha tinan 2014 nia rohan, bainhira ema halo obra ida iha Baukau, sira hetan derepente tambór ida ne'ebé kuaze kompletu, ho diámetru m 1,03, aas cm 78 no todan maizumenus kg 80. Arkeólogu Nuno Vasco Oliveira identifika nia hanesan tambór Dong Son ida ho idade tinan 2 000 ka liu, ida husi sira-ne'ebé di'ak liu iha Ázia Sudeste. Molok ne'e, ema hetan ona iha Timór-Leste tambór tipu hanesan, maibé aat tebes.
text.pt: Os tambores de Dong Son são grandes tambores de bronze feitos em oficinas do norte do Vietname e do sul da China; têm o nome de uma aldeia vietnamita onde esta cultura foi identificada pela primeira vez. A face de cima tem muitas vezes uma estrela ao centro, e os lados mostram aves, barcos e pessoas enfeitadas com penas. No fim de 2014, durante uma obra em Baucau, encontrou-se por acaso um tambor quase inteiro, com 1,03 m de diâmetro, 78 cm de altura e cerca de 80 kg. O arqueólogo Nuno Vasco Oliveira identificou-o como um tambor de Dong Son com pelo menos 2000 anos, um dos mais bem conservados do Sudeste Asiático. Antes dele, já tinham aparecido em Timor-Leste tambores do mesmo tipo, mas muito danificados.
text.en: Dong Son drums are large bronze drums made in workshops in northern Vietnam and southern China; they are named after a Vietnamese village where this culture was first identified. The top face often has a star in the centre, and the sides show birds, boats and people decorated with feathers. In late 2014, during building work in Baucau, an almost complete drum was found by chance, 1.03 m in diameter, 78 cm high and weighing about 80 kg. The archaeologist Nuno Vasco Oliveira identified it as a Dong Son drum at least 2,000 years old, one of the best preserved in Southeast Asia. Before it, drums of the same type had already been found in Timor-Leste, but they were badly damaged.
text.id: Nekara Dong Son adalah genderang perunggu besar yang dibuat di bengkel-bengkel di Vietnam utara dan Tiongkok selatan; namanya berasal dari sebuah desa di Vietnam tempat budaya ini pertama kali dikenali. Bidang atasnya sering memiliki bintang di tengah, dan sisi-sisinya menggambarkan burung, perahu, dan orang yang berhias bulu burung. Pada akhir 2014, saat pekerjaan pembangunan di Baucau, secara kebetulan ditemukan sebuah nekara yang hampir utuh, berdiameter 1,03 m, tinggi 78 cm, dan berat sekitar 80 kg. Arkeolog Nuno Vasco Oliveira mengenalinya sebagai nekara Dong Son yang berumur sedikitnya 2.000 tahun, salah satu yang paling utuh di Asia Tenggara. Sebelumnya, nekara dari jenis yang sama sudah pernah ditemukan di Timor-Leste, tetapi dalam keadaan rusak parah.

heading.tet: Testu dahuluk sira: Xina no Java
heading.pt: Os primeiros textos: China e Java
heading.en: The first texts: China and Java

text.tet: Testu tuan liu sira ne'ebé ko'alia kona-ba Timór, ema estranjeiru mak hakerek, tuir buat ne'ebé komersiante sira konta. Iha tinan 1225, Zhao Rugua, funsionáriu ida ba negósiu tasi nian iha portu Xina Quanzhou, hakerek Zhu Fan Zhi, livru ida kona-ba povu estranjeiru sira, ne'ebé temi Timór nia ai-kameli. Maizumenus tinan 1350, viajante Xina Wang Dayuan deskreve illa ne'e no oinsá ema troka ai-kameli ho osan-mutin, besi no hena. Iha tinan 1365, iha Java, poeta Prapanca remata Nagarakretagama, poema naruk ida atu hahi liurai Hayam Wuruk husi Majapahit, no poema ne'e tau Timór iha rai sira-nia lista ne'ebé liga ho reinu ne'e. Testu sira-ne'e hatudu katak ema iha rai dook hatene ona Timór, liuliu tanba ninia ai-kameli.
text.pt: Os textos mais antigos que falam de Timor foram escritos por estrangeiros, a partir do que contavam os mercadores. Em 1225, Zhao Rugua, funcionário do comércio marítimo no porto chinês de Quanzhou, escreveu o Zhu Fan Zhi, uma descrição dos povos estrangeiros que menciona o sândalo de Timor. Por volta de 1350, o viajante chinês Wang Dayuan descreveu a ilha e a troca de sândalo por prata, ferro e tecidos. Em 1365, em Java, o poeta Prapanca terminou o Nagarakretagama, um longo poema em honra do rei Hayam Wuruk, de Majapahit, que inclui Timor numa lista de terras ligadas ao reino. Estes textos mostram que Timor já era conhecida em terras distantes, sobretudo pelo seu sândalo.
text.en: The oldest texts that speak of Timor were written by foreigners, based on what traders told them. In 1225 Zhao Rugua, an official in charge of maritime trade at the Chinese port of Quanzhou, wrote the Zhu Fan Zhi, a description of foreign peoples that mentions Timor's sandalwood. Around 1350 the Chinese traveller Wang Dayuan described the island and the exchange of sandalwood for silver, iron and cloth. In 1365, in Java, the poet Prapanca completed the Nagarakretagama, a long poem in honour of King Hayam Wuruk of Majapahit, which includes Timor in a list of lands linked to the kingdom. These texts show that Timor was already known in distant lands, above all for its sandalwood.
text.id: Teks-teks tertua yang membicarakan Timor ditulis oleh orang asing, berdasarkan cerita para pedagang. Pada 1225, Zhao Rugua, pejabat urusan perdagangan laut di pelabuhan Quanzhou, Tiongkok, menulis Zhu Fan Zhi, sebuah uraian tentang bangsa-bangsa asing yang menyebut cendana Timor. Sekitar tahun 1350, pengelana Tiongkok Wang Dayuan menggambarkan pulau ini dan pertukaran cendana dengan perak, besi, dan kain. Pada 1365, di Jawa, pujangga Prapanca merampungkan Nagarakretagama, syair panjang untuk menghormati Raja Hayam Wuruk dari Majapahit, yang mencantumkan Timor dalam daftar negeri yang terkait dengan kerajaan itu. Teks-teks ini menunjukkan bahwa Timor sudah dikenal di negeri-negeri yang jauh, terutama karena cendananya.

text.tet: Iha 26 Janeiru 1522, ró Victoria, husi Fernão de Magalhães nia espedisaun, to'o Timór no hela to'o 11 Fevereiru; Magalhães mate ona, no Juan Sebastián Elcano mak ukun ró ne'e. Antonio Pigafetta, ema Itália ne'ebé hakerek viajen nia diáriu, husik hela deskrisaun dahuluk husi ema Europa ida ne'ebé to'o duni illa ne'e; uluk ne'e, entre 1512 no 1515, Tomé Pires hakerek ona kona-ba Timór iha Malaka, tuir buat ne'ebé nia rona. Pigafetta konta katak ró nia ema sira, ho hamlaha, kaer xefe lokál ida to'o sira simu karau, bibi no fahi. Nia hakerek katak ai-kameli mutin iha de'it iha ne'ebá, no nia tau iha lista ai-lia, hare, hudi, tohu, sabraka no kakatua. Nia ko'alia kona-ba liurai na'in haat, ho sira-nia fatin iha Oibich, Lichsana, Suai no Cabanaza, no nia haree ró boot ida (junku) husi Luzon, iha Filipinas, ne'ebé mai buka ai-kameli.
text.pt: A 26 de janeiro de 1522, o navio Victoria, da expedição de Fernão de Magalhães, chegou a Timor e ficou até 11 de fevereiro; Magalhães já tinha morrido e o comandante era Juan Sebastián Elcano. O italiano Antonio Pigafetta, autor do diário da viagem, deixou a primeira descrição da ilha feita por um europeu que lá esteve; antes, entre 1512 e 1515, Tomé Pires escrevera sobre Timor em Malaca, a partir do que ouvia. Pigafetta contou que a tripulação, com fome, reteve um chefe local até receber búfalos, cabras e porcos. Escreveu que o sândalo branco só existia ali e listou gengibre, arroz, bananas, cana-de-açúcar, laranjas e papagaios. Falou de quatro reis, com sede em Oibich, Lichsana, Suai e Cabanaza, e viu um junco de Luzon, nas Filipinas, que viera buscar sândalo.
text.en: On 26 January 1522 the ship Victoria, of Ferdinand Magellan's expedition, reached Timor and stayed until 11 February; Magellan had already died, and the commander was Juan Sebastián Elcano. The Italian Antonio Pigafetta, who wrote the diary of the voyage, left the first description of the island by a European who had been there; earlier, between 1512 and 1515, Tomé Pires had written about Timor in Malacca, based on what he heard. Pigafetta related that the hungry crew held a local chief until they received buffaloes, goats and pigs. He wrote that white sandalwood was found only there and listed ginger, rice, bananas, sugar cane, oranges and parrots. He spoke of four kings, based at Oibich, Lichsana, Suai and Cabanaza, and saw a junk from Luzon, in the Philippines, that had come for sandalwood.
text.id: Pada 26 Januari 1522, kapal Victoria dari ekspedisi Ferdinand Magelhaens tiba di Timor dan tinggal sampai 11 Februari; Magelhaens sudah meninggal, dan komandannya adalah Juan Sebastián Elcano. Antonio Pigafetta, orang Italia yang menulis catatan harian pelayaran itu, meninggalkan uraian pertama tentang pulau ini yang dibuat oleh orang Eropa yang pernah berada di sana; sebelumnya, antara 1512 dan 1515, Tomé Pires sudah menulis tentang Timor di Malaka, berdasarkan apa yang didengarnya. Pigafetta menceritakan bahwa awak kapal yang kelaparan menahan seorang kepala setempat sampai mereka menerima kerbau, kambing, dan babi. Ia menulis bahwa cendana putih hanya ada di sana dan mencatat jahe, padi, pisang, tebu, jeruk, dan burung nuri. Ia menyebut empat raja, yang berkedudukan di Oibich, Lichsana, Suai, dan Cabanaza, dan melihat sebuah jung dari Luzon, Filipina, yang datang untuk mencari cendana.

heading.tet: Fonte sira ne'ebé presiza lee ho kuidadu
heading.id: Sumber yang harus dibaca dengan hati-hati

text.tet: Rejistu dahuluk sira-ne'e folin-boot, maibé presiza lee ho kuidadu. Vizitante sira mak hakerek sira; vizitante sira-ne'e hela tempu badak, la ko'alia lian lokál sira no sira interese liuliu ba negósiu. Naran balu ne'ebé Pigafetta hakerek hanesan fó hanoin ba fatin ohin loron nian, hanesan Likisá no Suai, maibé istoriadór sira sei diskute ligasaun sira-ne'e. Timoroan sira mós iha sira-nia memória rasik: istória orijen nian, bei'ala sira-nia naran no uma lulik nia tradisaun, ne'ebé lia-na'in sira rai no hato'o ho ibun. Arkeolojia, testu tuan no tradisaun orál kompleta malu. Iha tempu ne'e, ró Portugés sira mai ona husi Malaka atu buka ai-kameli, desde maizumenus 1515, no tempu foun ida iha Timór nia istória hahú.
text.pt: Estes primeiros registos são preciosos, mas devem ser lidos com cuidado. Foram escritos por visitantes que ficaram pouco tempo, não falavam as línguas locais e se interessavam sobretudo pelo comércio. Alguns nomes que Pigafetta escreveu parecem lembrar lugares atuais, como Liquiçá e Suai, mas os historiadores ainda discutem essas ligações. Os timorenses tinham também a sua própria memória: histórias de origem, genealogias e tradições das casas sagradas, guardadas pelos lia-na'in e transmitidas oralmente. A arqueologia, os textos antigos e a tradição oral completam-se. Nessa altura, navios portugueses já vinham de Malaca buscar sândalo, desde cerca de 1515, e começava uma nova época da história de Timor.
text.en: These first records are precious, but they must be read with care. They were written by visitors who stayed only a short time, did not speak the local languages and were interested mainly in trade. Some names that Pigafetta wrote down seem to recall places of today, such as Liquiçá and Suai, but historians still debate these links. The Timorese also had their own memory: origin stories, genealogies and the traditions of the sacred houses, kept by the lia-na'in and passed on by word of mouth. Archaeology, old texts and oral tradition complete one another. By that time Portuguese ships had already been coming from Malacca for sandalwood, since about 1515, and a new era in the history of Timor was beginning.
text.id: Catatan-catatan pertama ini sangat berharga, tetapi harus dibaca dengan hati-hati. Catatan itu ditulis oleh pengunjung yang hanya tinggal sebentar, tidak berbicara bahasa setempat, dan terutama tertarik pada perdagangan. Beberapa nama yang ditulis Pigafetta tampak mirip dengan tempat-tempat masa kini, seperti Liquiçá dan Suai, tetapi para sejarawan masih memperdebatkan hubungan itu. Orang Timor juga memiliki ingatan mereka sendiri: kisah asal-usul, silsilah, dan tradisi rumah-rumah adat yang sakral, yang dijaga oleh para lia-na'in dan diwariskan secara lisan. Arkeologi, teks-teks lama, dan tradisi lisan saling melengkapi. Pada masa itu, kapal-kapal Portugis sudah datang dari Malaka untuk mencari cendana sejak sekitar 1515, dan dimulailah zaman baru dalam sejarah Timor.

review.notes: Baucau Dong Son drum: found by chance at a construction site in late 2014; 1.03 m diameter, 78 cm high, about 80 kg; identified by Nuno Vasco Oliveira; at least 2,000 years old (Vietnamese press, e.g. Hanoi Times). The press says earlier, badly damaged drums had been found; the Antiquity paper (Oliveira, O'Connor, Bellwood) reports two drums from Timor-Leste — check the total number. Drum decoration (central star, birds, boats, feathered figures) and the name from a Vietnamese village are general knowledge. West Timor copper source and possible local copper/bronze working: Antiquity abstract. Zhao Rugua (maritime trade official, Quanzhou, 1225), Wang Dayuan (c. 1350) and the Nagarakretagama (Prapanca, 1365, for Hayam Wuruk) are general knowledge, consistent with tl.history.sandalwood_trade. PIGAFETTA DETAILS ARE FROM MEMORY of his account (Robertson translation), not confirmed by search: Victoria under Elcano at Timor 26 Jan–11 Feb 1522 (the crew's calendar was one day behind after crossing the Pacific); a chief held until buffaloes, goats and pigs were delivered; white sandalwood only there; ginger, rice, bananas, sugar cane, oranges, parrots; four kings at Oibich, Lichsana, Suai and Cabanaza; a junk from Luzon trading for sandalwood — check all. Links of Lichsana/Suai to Liquiçá/Suai are said to be debated. Tomé Pires (Suma Oriental, 1512–1515) wrote about Timor from Malacca without visiting (see tl.history.sandalwood_trade), hence 'first description by a European who was there' for Pigafetta. Period: about 1 CE (drums at least 2,000 years old) to 1522. Timeline 1225, 1350 and 1365 reuse the titles of tl.history.sandalwood_trade on purpose. Tetun terms to check: Illa Sunda Ki'ik, pulseira, kobre, estañu, junku, ai-lia (ginger), sabraka, kakatua, manu-fulun, lia-na'in, Quanzhou, hahi (praise). EN/ID (2026-11-11): English and Indonesian translated by hand from the Portuguese and checked against the Tetun; Tetun and Portuguese not changed. Timeline titles shared between articles are translated identically. Terms (en/id): Dong Son drum/nekara (genderang perunggu), socketed axe/kapak corong, Lesser Sunda Islands/Kepulauan Sunda Kecil, the poet Prapanca/pujangga Prapanca (Indonesian books often write 'Mpu Prapanca'), junk/jung, Magellan/Magelhaens. A 2026-11-11 web search did not find Pigafetta's passage on the four kings, so the Pigafetta details above are still unverified.
